proposed: Shared neoantigens can arise from driver hotspot mutations, such as a TP53 hotspot mutation, and neoantigens from frequent driver mutations might be shared by patients with various types of cancers.
why: Dropped BRAF V600E, KRAS and TP53 R175H specifics and 'critical genes'. Quote 0 gives a shared neoantigen from a TP53 hotspot mutation; quote 1 gives hedged sharing across patients.

evidence.quote: In this issue, Kim and colleagues report the first successful application of TCR gene therapy targeting a shared, or public, neoantigen resulting from a TP53 hotspot mutation.

Since the identified neoantigens might be shared by patients with various types of cancers and are not easily lost due to immune escape, they have the potential to be promising off-the-shelf cancer immunotherapy targets in patients with the corresponding mutations.

original: Similarly, HER2/neu (ERBB2) shows dramatic overexpression in approximately 20-25% of breast cancers, making it a successful therapeutic target.
proposed: Similarly, HER2-positive breast cancer accounts for approximately 15-20% of breast cancer cases and is a crucial focus in the treatment of breast cancer.
why: Replaced the 20-25% overexpression figure with the quote's 15-20% HER2-positive share, and 'successful target' with 'crucial focus of treatment'.

evidence.quote: Among breast cancer cases, the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer accounts for 15% to 20% and is a crucial focus in the treatment of breast cancer.

original: The MAGE (melanoma-associated antigen) family and NY-ESO-1 are among the most extensively studied CTAs, and their expression across multiple tumor types has made them targets for therapeutic vaccines and adoptive T-cell therapies.
proposed: MAGE-A4 and NY-ESO-1 are cancer/testis antigens expressed in multiple solid tumors or broadly across cancer types, and NY-ESO-1 is described as an attractive therapeutic target because of its restricted expression in normal tissues; MAGE-A4 is targeted by the adoptive T cell therapy afami-cel.
why: Dropped 'most extensively studied', the whole MAGE family and therapeutic vaccines. Quote 0 gives MAGE-A4 expression and afami-cel; quote 1 gives NY-ESO-1 expression and target status.

evidence.quote: Afamitresgene autoleucel (afami-cel) is a human leukocyte antigen-restricted autologous T cell therapy targeting melanoma-associated antigen A4 (MAGE-A4), a cancer/testis antigen expressed at varying levels in multiple solid tumors.
NY-ESO-1, a human cancer-testis antigen, represents an attractive target for such therapies due to its broad expression in different cancer types and the restricted expression in normal tissues.

original: The success of prophylactic vaccines against HPV and HBV in preventing virus-associated cancers demonstrates the therapeutic potential of targeting oncoviral antigens.
proposed: HPV vaccination prevents cervical, head and neck, and anogenital cancers.
why: Dropped HBV and the broader claim about demonstrating therapeutic potential of oncoviral antigens; the quote only states HPV vaccination prevents these cancers.

evidence.quote: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents cervical, head and neck, and anogenital cancers.

original: B-cell-mediated tumour promotion has been shown to involve different mechanisms, such as production of immunosuppressive cytokines (IL-10) and/or production of antibodies and formation of immune complexes that skew TAMs in an M2-like direction.
proposed: B-cell-mediated tumour promotion has been shown to involve production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as IL-10; in one study, B1 lymphocytes expressing IL-10 played a key role in promoting a pro-tumoral M2-biased phenotype of macrophages.
why: Dropped antibody and immune-complex route, which the quote does not state. Quote 0 supports IL-10-expressing B1 cells driving M2-biased macrophages.

evidence.quote: In this issue of the European Journal of Immunology, a study demonstrates that B1 lymphocytes expressing IL-10 play a key role in promoting a pro-tumoral M2-biased phenotype of macrophages.

original: Infiltration of TAMs is generally associated with worse prognosis, which is a reflection of their pro-tumour function.
proposed: Infiltration of some macrophage subpopulations has been linked to tumor recurrence, for example TREM2/APOE/C1Q-positive macrophage infiltration as a potential prognostic biomarker for ccRCC recurrence, and M2 macrophages promoted the proliferation, invasion and migration of prostate cancer cells.
why: Dropped 'TAM infiltration generally worse prognosis'. Quote 0 carries the ccRCC recurrence biomarker; quote 1 carries pro-tumor effects of M2 macrophages in prostate cancer.

evidence.quote: The study thus identifies TREM2/APOE/C1Q-positive macrophage infiltration as a potential prognostic biomarker for ccRCC recurrence, as well as a candidate therapeutic target.
CCK8, Transwell invasion, and wound healing further verified that M2 macrophages promoted the proliferation, invasion, and migration of PCa (p < 0.05).

original: Natural killer cells are innate lymphoid cells that have long been considered to play a role in resistance against haematogenous dissemination of cancer cells, in particular to the lungs.
proposed: Natural killer cells have been shown to mediate resistance to haematogenous metastasis to the lungs and liver in experimental studies, including a study in which NK-cell depletion almost abolished the reduced lung metastasis of breast cancer seen with GRh2.
why: Dropped innate lymphoid cell classification and 'long considered'. Quote 0: NK-cell-mediated resistance to haematogenous liver and lung metastasis; quote 1: NK depletion abolished reduced lung metastasis.

evidence.quote: Its genetic blockade unleashes NK-cell-mediated resistance to hepatic carcinogenesis, haematogenous liver and lung metastasis, and cytomegalovirus infection.
Importantly, the reduced lung metastasis of breast cancer by GRh2 was almost abolished upon the depletion of NK cells.

original: NK cells have granules with perforins and granzymes that act on target cells inducing lysis or apoptosis and also express PRRs including TLR-2, -3, -4, -5, -7, and -8.
proposed: NK cells express Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2), and in one study granzyme A was found to be mainly expressed by NK cells among lymphoid cells.
why: Dropped perforins, lysis/apoptosis and TLR-3, -4, -5, -7, -8, which no quote states. Quote 0 carries TLR2 on NK cells; quote 1 carries granzyme A expression.

evidence.quote: Mechanistically, lipoteichoic acid (LTA) within SA-EVs engaged Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) on NK cells, activating MyD88/NF-κB signalling pathway.
Analysis of GzmA in lymphoid cells following CLP showed that it was mainly expressed by NK cells.

original: AICD is considered to be one of the mechanisms responsible for the increased apoptotic rate among TILs.
proposed: AICD has been observed in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes: TNF-mediated AICD occurred in tumor-infiltrating CD8 T lymphocytes, and in another study TIL rapidly died by AICD upon activation in vitro and in vivo.
why: Dropped the claim that AICD accounts for the increased apoptotic rate among TILs in situ; quote 1 notes TIL were not shown dying in situ. Quote 0 gives TNF-mediated AICD in TILs.

evidence.quote: TNF-mediated AICD was also observed upon activation of virus-specific CD8 T cells and tumor-infiltrating CD8 T lymphocytes.

Our data demonstrate that TIL, not tumor, express both Fas and FasL, are arrested in G(1), do not secrete cytokine in situ, and, upon activation in vitro and in vivo, rapidly die by activation-induced cell death.

original: Dysfunctional immune responses can result as some tumor cells express Fas ligand (FasL) and bind Fas expressed on some infiltrating lymphocytes resulting in AICD seems to be differentially regulated in T-helper subsets.
proposed: Dysfunctional immune responses can result when FasL expressed by cells in the tumor microenvironment, including endothelial cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, triggers apoptosis of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes; FasL has also been discussed as an effector molecule for immune privilege and tumour survival.
why: Replaced tumor-cell FasL with endothelial cells and MDSCs; dropped T-helper subset regulation. Quote 0 gives FasL killing of TIL; quote 1 gives immune privilege and tumour survival.

evidence.quote: Recent evidence indicates that other cells in the tumor microenvironment can express FasL and trigger apoptosis of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL), including endothelial cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells.
Moreover, FasL is discussed as direct effector molecule for the establishment of immune privilege and tumour survival.

original: Over the past decade, a number of reports have provided data indicating that tumor cells can either directly produce PGs or induce macrophages in the tumor microenvironment to secrete PGs.
proposed: A number of reports indicate that tumor cells can produce immunosuppressive prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), and elevated COX1/2 expression has been reported in TAMs in MSS tumors compared with MSI tumors.
why: Dropped 'over the past decade' and macrophage induction by tumor cells. Quote 0 carries tumor cell-derived PGE2; quote 1 carries COX1/2 expression in TAMs.

evidence.quote: These immunosuppressive events are mediated by tumor cell derived fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) and prostaglandin E2 (PGE2).
Transcriptomic analysis revealed elevated COX1/2 expression in TAMs in MSS tumors compared with MSI tumors.

original: Overexpression of COX-2 results in increased production of PGs by tumor cells and, in the case of PGE2, results in an upregulation of antiapoptotic proteins, such as Bcl-2, in tumor cells.
proposed: In cancer cells, PGE2 can upregulate the antiapoptotic protein Bcl-2, as in human colon cancer (HCA-7) cells, and in gastric cancer cells PTGS2 mediated cisplatin-induced BCL2 expression through the PGE2/EP4 axis.
why: Dropped COX-2 overexpression raising PG production, which no quote states directly. Quote 0 gives PGE2 inducing Bcl-2 in colon cancer cells; quote 1 gives PTGS2-driven BCL2 expression in gastric cancer cells.

evidence.quote: Additionally, PGE2 inhibits programmed cell death caused by SC-58125 and induces Bcl-2 expression, but did not affect Bcl-x or Bax expression in human colon cancer (HCA-7) cells.
In addition, PTGS2 mediated cisplatin-induced BCL2 expression and subsequent resistance to apoptosis via PGE2/EP4/MAPKs (ERK1/2, P38) axis.

original: Rapidly growing tumor cells require nutrients, oxygen, and essential metabolites to proliferate and, at the same time, create an immunosuppressive microenvironment.
proposed: The tumor microenvironment is immunosuppressive and is characterized by metabolic restrictions such as low glucose levels, a low pH, and hypoxia.
why: Dropped tumor cells' nutrient and oxygen requirements, which no quote states. Quote 0 lists low glucose, low pH, hypoxia; quote 1 lists hypoxia and acidity as immunosuppressive TME features.

evidence.quote: Therapeutics that target metabolic restrictions, such as low glucose levels, a low pH, hypoxia and the generation of suppressive metabolites, have shown promise as combination therapies for different types of cancer.

Initial research has uncovered immunosuppressive properties of the TME, which include low oxygen levels (hypoxia), acidic conditions (low pH), increased interstitial pressure, heightened permeability of tumor vasculature, and an inflammatory microenvironment.

original: The pathway responsible for these effects has recently been elucidated as being a consequence of cyclooxygenase (COX) overexpression in cancer cells, particularly COX-2.
proposed: In an immunogenic murine lung cancer model, oncogenic KRAS was found to promote immune evasion most notably via upregulation of immunosuppressive COX2 in cancer cells, and tumor production of PGE2 has been linked to evasion of the NK cell-cDC1 axis.
why: Narrowed to one KRAS-driven murine lung cancer model; dropped 'recently elucidated pathway' and general COX overexpression. Quote 0 carries COX2 upregulation; quote 1 carries tumor PGE2 and immune evasion.

evidence.quote: In vivo CRISPR-Cas9 screening in an immunogenic murine lung cancer model identified mechanisms by which oncogenic KRAS promotes immune evasion, most notably via upregulation of immunosuppressive COX2 in cancer cells.

Notably, tumor production of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) leads to evasion of the NK cell-cDC1 axis in part by impairing NK cell viability and chemokine production, as well as by causing downregulation of chemokine receptor expression in cDC1.

original: The tumor microenvironment physically constitutes a barrier against T-cell infiltration, as it is a compact structure with tight interactions among cancer cells, fibroblasts, immune cells, and ECM.
proposed: The tumor microenvironment can form a physical barrier against T-cell infiltration: in one study, interactions among tumor cells, macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts stimulated deposition and entanglement of collagen fibers at tumor boundaries, obstructing T cell infiltration, and a fibroblast-macrophage interaction might stimulate an immune-excluded desmoplastic structure that limits T cell infiltration.
why: Dropped 'compact structure with tight interactions' as flat fact. Quote 0 carries the collagen barrier at tumor boundaries; quote 1 carries the hedged desmoplastic structure limiting T cell infiltration.

evidence.quote: We find that tumor cells and secreted phosphoprotein 1-positive macrophages interact with collagen type XI alpha 1 chain-positive cancer-associated fibroblasts to stimulate the deposition and entanglement of collagen fibers at tumor boundaries, obstructing T cell infiltration and leading to poor prognosis.
This interaction might be regulated by chemerin, TGF-β, and interleukin-1, which would stimulate the formation of immune-excluded desmoplasic structure and limit the T cell infiltration.

original: There is ample evidence that tumor cells produce immunosuppressive factors, and this has been verified to have local as well as systemic effects on immune function.
proposed: Tumor cells produce immunosuppressive factors such as exosomal PD-L1, which suppresses T cell activation in the draining lymph node, and systemically introduced exosomal PD-L1 rescues growth of tumors unable to secrete their own.
why: Replaced 'ample evidence...verified' with one documented example showing local and systemic effects. Dropped IL-35, since quote 1 does not say it is immunosuppressive.

evidence.quote: Exosomal PD-L1 from the tumor suppresses T cell activation in the draining lymph node. Systemically introduced exosomal PD-L1 rescues growth of tumors unable to secrete their own.

original: Acquired resistance develops through various mechanisms including loss of target antigens, evolution of less immunogenic tumor clones, and upregulation of alternative immune checkpoints.
proposed: Resistance to immunotherapy appears to involve mechanisms that broadly overlap with those used by cancers during immunoediting, in which tumour immunogenicity is edited and immunosuppressive mechanisms that enable disease progression are acquired.
why: Dropped antigen loss, less immunogenic clones and alternative checkpoints, which are not named. Quote 0 states resistance mechanisms seem to broadly overlap with immunoediting mechanisms.

evidence.quote: Throughout these phases, tumour immunogenicity is edited, and immunosuppressive mechanisms that enable disease progression are acquired. The mechanisms of resistance to immunotherapy seem to broadly overlap with those used by cancers as they undergo immunoediting to evade detection by the immune system.

original: CAR T cells combined with checkpoint blockade (particularly anti-PD-1) represent a rational combination, as checkpoint inhibitors can counteract the exhaustion that CAR T cells undergo within the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.
proposed: Combining CAR T cells with checkpoint blockade has been proposed as a way to address tumor microenvironment-induced T cell exhaustion, and anti-PD-1 therapy can possibly reverse CAR T cell exhaustion in DLBCL.
why: Dropped 'particularly anti-PD-1' as a general rule and the flat statement that checkpoint inhibitors counteract exhaustion. Quote 0 is hedged ('can possibly'); quote 1 proposes combining CAR-T with checkpoint blockade.

evidence.quote: Anti-PD-1 therapy can possibly reverse CAR T cells exhaustion in DLBCL.

The TME sets major obstacles for CAR-T therapies, creating conditions that suppress the immune response, inducing T cell exhaustion. To enhance treatment efficacy, specific efforts associated with CAR-T cell therapy in NSCLC, should definitely focus TME-related immunosuppression and antigen escape mechanisms, by combining CAR-T cells with immune checkpoint blockades.

original: Clinical trials combining CAR T cells targeting mesothelin, EGFRvIII, or other solid tumor antigens with pembrolizumab or other checkpoint inhibitors are ongoing in glioblastoma, mesothelioma, and other solid tumors.
proposed: Clinical trials combining T-cell therapies with pembrolizumab have been registered, including an open-label phase 1 study of EGFRvIII T cells with pembrolizumab in newly diagnosed EGFRvIII+, MGMT-unmethylated glioblastoma and a phase 2 study part testing a study treatment with pembrolizumab in malignant pleural mesothelioma.
why: Dropped 'ongoing' and the mesothelin, other antigens and other solid tumor claims. Quote 1 is a record now marked completed; quote 0 shows a mesothelioma pembrolizumab combination.

evidence.quote: Phase 2 part of the study, the investigators will test the dose in combination with another drug, pembrolizumab, to see what effects the study treatment has on malignant pleural mesothelioma.

This is an open-label, phase 1 study to assess the safety and tolerability of EGFRvIII T cells in combination with pembrolizumab (PD-1 Inhibitor) in patients with newly diagnosed, EGFRvIII+, MGMT-unmethylated glioblastoma.

original: Mechanisms of primary resistance include lack of neoantigen expression, defects in antigen presentation machinery, absence of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, and intrinsic immunosuppression within the tumor microenvironment.
proposed: One mechanism of primary resistance is a lack of immune infiltration: cold tumors, which lack immune infiltration, remain resistant to therapy, in contrast to hot tumors that respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
why: Reduced the list to lack of immune infiltration; neoantigen lack, antigen presentation defects and intrinsic immunosuppression are not stated in quote 0.

evidence.quote: Hot tumors, characterized by heightened immune activity and responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), stand in stark contrast to cold tumors, which lack immune infiltration and remain resistant to therapy.

original: Novel immune checkpoint targets beyond PD-1 and CTLA-4—including LAG-3, TIM-3, TIGIT, and VISTA—are being evaluated in clinical trials, either as monotherapies or in combination with established checkpoint inhibitors, with the goal of overcoming resistance mechanisms.
proposed: Immune checkpoint targets beyond PD-1 and CTLA-4, such as LAG-3 and TIM-3, have been evaluated in clinical trials, including a phase IIR trial with an anti-LAG3 arm and a phase 1b trial of an anti-PD-1 antibody combined with either an anti-LAG-3 or an anti-TIM-3 antibody.
why: Dropped TIGIT, VISTA, 'monotherapy' and the resistance goal; trial records are dated, one completed, so past tense. Quote 0 carries the anti-LAG3 arm; quote 1 carries the PD-1 plus LAG-3/TIM-3 trial.

evidence.quote: This is a multicentre, phase IIR, double non-comparative arm trial, with an initial safety run for the anti-LAG3 arm.

An Exploratory, Open-label, Multicenter Phase 1b Trial to Evaluate Safety and Efficacy of Sym021 (Anti-PD 1) in Combination With Either Sym022 (Anti-LAG-3) or Sym023 (Anti-TIM-3) or Sym023 and Irinotecan

original: Oncolytic viruses, which selectively infect and lyse tumor cells while releasing tumor antigens and damage-associated molecular patterns, can convert "cold" non-inflamed tumors into "hot" inflamed tumors that become responsive to checkpoint inhibitors.
proposed: Oncolytic viruses can modulate the microenvironment of tumors with low pre-existing immune cell infiltration, which respond poorly to checkpoint therapies, making them attractive agents for combination with checkpoint inhibitors; an editorial proposes that the TGF-β trap of AdAPT-001 makes tumors susceptible to anti-PD-1 therapy.
why: Dropped selective infection, lysis, antigen release, and the flat 'convert cold to hot'. Quote 0 carries microenvironment modulation for poorly infiltrated tumors; quote 1 is a proposal for AdAPT-001.

evidence.quote: Tumors with a low level of pre-existing immune cell infiltration respond poorly to immune checkpoint therapies. Oncolytic viruses optimize immunotherapies by modulating the tumor microenvironment and affecting multiple steps in the cancer-immunity cycle, making them an attractive agent for combination strategies.

This editorial proposes that the TGF-β trap of AdAPT-001 reverses the immunosuppressive environment of tumor cells, and thus makes these tumors susceptible to CIs like the anti-PD-1 agent, nivolumab, and potentially other therapies as well.

original: PD-L1 expression on tumor cells, tumor mutational burden (TMB), microsatellite instability, deficient mismatch repair, and inflammatory gene expression signatures all serve as predictive biomarkers for checkpoint inhibitor response, although none are perfectly predictive.
proposed: PD-L1 expression, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and high-frequency microsatellite instability/deficient mismatch repair (MSI-H/dMMR) are used as biomarkers in selecting patients for checkpoint inhibitor treatment, although further validation is needed.
why: Dropped inflammatory gene signatures and 'predictive' wording. Quote 0 carries PD-L1 and TMB with further validation needed; quote 1 carries MSI-H/dMMR for checkpoint inhibitor eligibility.

evidence.quote: Biomarkers such as PD-L1 expression, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and Human Papillomavirus (HPV) status play a critical role in treatment selection, but further validation is needed.
High-frequency MSI (MSI-H)/dMMR is gaining increasing interest as a biomarker for advanced cancer patients to determine their eligibility for immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs).

original: Personalized neoantigen vaccines require complex manufacturing workflows, face challenges in accurately predicting immunogenic neoantigens (high false-positive rates in computational predictions), and must overcome tumor heterogeneity where not all cancer cells express the targeted neoantigens.
proposed: AI-powered cancer vaccines face significant challenges, such as tumor heterogeneity and genetic variability, which can limit the effectiveness of neoantigen prediction, and reviews of neoantigen vaccines point to obstacles in vaccine design and the tumour environment.
why: Dropped manufacturing complexity and false-positive rates, not in the quotes. Quote 0 names heterogeneity and variability limiting prediction; quote 1 notes obstacles in vaccine design and the tumour environment.

evidence.quote: Despite the promise of AI-powered cancer vaccines, significant challenges remain, such as tumor heterogeneity and genetic variability, which can limit the effectiveness of neoantigen prediction.

In this Review, we focus on the key obstacles pertaining to vaccine design and tumour environment that remain to be overcome in order to unleash the true potential of neoantigen vaccines in cancer therapy.

original: Preclinical studies have demonstrated that PD-1 inhibition combined with CAR T cells results in decreased myeloid-derived suppressor cell accumulation in tumors, reduced CAR T-cell exhaustion, and enhanced anti-tumor efficacy.
proposed: Some studies suggest that anti-PD-1 therapy can possibly reverse CAR T cell exhaustion in DLBCL, and in multiple SCLC models the reduced exhaustion and durable responses of IL-18-secreting anti-DLL3 CAR T cells could be further enhanced with anti-PD-1 blockade.
why: Dropped decreased MDSC accumulation and the general 'demonstrated' claim. Quote 0 is hedged on reversing exhaustion in DLBCL; quote 1 gives less exhaustion and enhancement with anti-PD-1 in SCLC models.

evidence.quote: Anti-PD-1 therapy can possibly reverse CAR T cells exhaustion in DLBCL.

Additionally, human IL-18-secreting anti-DLL3 CAR T cells showed an increased memory phenotype, less exhaustion, and induced durable responses in multiple SCLC models, an effect that could be further enhanced with anti-PD-1 blockade.

original: Predicted neoantigens are prioritized based on multiple factors including mutation expression level, predicted MHC binding affinity, peptide processing probability, and foreignness relative to normal sequences.
proposed: Predicted neoantigens are prioritized by integrating diverse data, including mutant allele expression, peptide binding affinities, and whether a mutation is clonal or subclonal, and peptide novelty metrics comparing tumor peptides with normal peptide sequences have been proposed to refine predicted neoantigenicity.
why: Replaced peptide processing probability with clonality; foreignness appears only as proposed novelty metrics. Quote 0 lists expression, affinity and clonality; quote 1 proposes the novelty metrics.

evidence.quote: Prioritization of predicted peptides occurs by integrating diverse data, including mutant allele expression, peptide binding affinities, and determination whether a mutation is clonal or subclonal.

We propose four peptide novelty metrics to refine predicted neoantigenicity: tumor vs. paired normal peptide binding affinity difference, tumor vs. paired normal peptide sequence similarity, tumor vs. closest human peptide sequence similarity, and tumor vs. closest microbial peptide sequence similarity.

original: Selected neoantigens are then synthesized as peptides, encoded in mRNA or DNA vectors, or loaded onto autologous dendritic cells for patient vaccination, often in combination with adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity.
proposed: Cancer vaccines can use platforms such as synthetic peptides, mRNA, DNA, and cellular vaccines, which have been reported to enhance antigen presentation and immune activation.
why: Dropped autologous dendritic cell loading and adjuvants, and the tie to selected neoantigens, which the quote does not state. Quote 0 lists the vaccine platforms.

evidence.quote: Recent advancements in vaccine platforms, such as synthetic peptides, mRNA, DNA, cellular, and nano-vaccines, have enhanced antigen presentation and immune activation.

original: The most successful CAR T-cell products target CD19, a B-cell lineage marker, achieving complete remission rates exceeding 80% in pediatric and young adult ALL, with many responses proving durable.
proposed: In one study of pediatric and young adult ALL, a CAR T-cell product achieved an overall remission rate of 81% within 3 months, with all responders negative for minimal residual disease.
why: Dropped CD19, the 80% threshold, and durability, which the quote does not state. The quote gives 81% overall remission within 3 months and MRD negativity in responders; the setting comes from the evidence note.

evidence.quote: The overall remission rate within 3 months was 81%, with all patients who had a response to treatment found to be negative for minimal residual disease, as assessed by means of flow cytometry.

original: Unleashing the anti-tumor potential of innate immune cells—particularly NK cells—through checkpoint blockade (targeting NKG2A or KIR receptors), cytokine stimulation, or engineered NK cell products is being actively pursued.
proposed: Expanded, activated NK cell infusions are being tested in clinical trials, for example with anti-GD2 antibody in neuroblastoma and after trastuzumab in HER2-positive breast or gastric cancer.
why: Dropped checkpoint blockade (NKG2A, KIR) and cytokine stimulation; the two trial records only describe engineered/expanded NK cell infusion studies. Quote 0 and 1 name the settings.

evidence.quote: We postulate that infusion of expanded activated NK cells from healthy haploidentical donors along with anti-GD2 antibody will enhance neuroblastoma killing.
This study will determine the safety and efficacy of expanded activated autologous NK cells administered after Trastuzumab in patients with HER2-positive breast or gastric cancer.

original: Much of the burden of cancer in the United States can be traced to modifiable health behaviors that increase one's risk of disease.
proposed: Much of the burden of cancer in the United States was attributable to the evaluated risk factors: an estimated 40.0% of incident cancers and 44.0% of cancer deaths in adults aged 30 and older in 2019, and 42.0% of cancers in 2014.
why: Dropped 'modifiable health behaviors', which neither quote states; quotes give only the share attributable to the evaluated risk factors (2019 and 2014 figures).

evidence.quote: In 2019, an estimated 40.0% (713,340 of 1,781,649) of all incident cancers (excluding nonmelanoma skin cancers) and 44.0% (262,120 of 595,737) of all cancer deaths in adults aged 30 years and older in the United States were attributable to the evaluated risk factors.

In the United States in 2014, an estimated 42.0% of all incident cancers (659,640 of 1570,975 cancers, excluding nonmelanoma skin cancers) and 45.1% of cancer deaths (265,150 of 587,521 deaths) were attributable to evaluated risk factors.

original: A major limitation is that many observational studies reporting dramatic cancer risk reductions were subsequently shown to be affected by time-related biases (particularly immortal time bias) that greatly exaggerate drug benefits.
proposed: A major limitation is that immortal time bias continues to distort many observational studies on metformin use and cancer risk.
why: Narrowed from many drugs and 'greatly exaggerate' to the quote's statement about metformin studies; dropped 'dramatic risk reductions' and 'subsequently shown'.

evidence.quote: Immortal time bias (ITB) continues to distort many observational studies on metformin use and cancer risk.

original: Broader Pattern of Failure: Chemoprevention of cancer has been characterized by some as "an almost universal failure"—not only producing null results but frequently showing excess disease, including the very diseases the agents were specifically chosen to prevent.
proposed: Chemoprevention trials can produce null results; for example, in one 12-month placebo-controlled trial, oral nicotinamide did not lead to lower numbers of keratinocyte cancers or actinic keratoses in immunosuppressed solid-organ transplant recipients.
why: Dropped the 'almost universal failure' characterization and excess disease, which the quote does not support. Kept one documented null trial and its setting.

evidence.quote: In this 12-month, placebo-controlled trial, oral nicotinamide therapy did not lead to lower numbers of keratinocyte cancers or actinic keratoses in immunosuppressed solid-organ transplant recipients.

original: Clinical Development: Randomized clinical trials have demonstrated significant activity of retinoids in reversing oral leukoplakia, a premalignant lesion associated with tobacco use and squamous cell carcinoma risk in the aerodigestive tract.
proposed: Randomized evidence on reversing oral leukoplakia is mixed: in one trial, complete regression rates were 52% with vitamin A and 33% with beta carotene versus 10% with placebo, whereas a meta-analysis of randomized trials found no significant difference in clinical response between chemopreventive agents and placebo in oral premalignant lesions.
why: Replaced 'demonstrated significant activity of retinoids' with the mixed picture: quote 0 shows vitamin A/beta carotene beating placebo; quote 1 shows no significant difference overall. Dropped tobacco and squamous cell risk framing.

evidence.quote: The complete regression rates were: 10% in the placebo arm, 52% with vitamin A and 33% with beta carotene (P < 0.0001).
The results suggested that there were no significant differences in comparing clinical responses between chemopreventive agents with placebo in treatment of OPLs.

original: Clinical Evidence and Challenges: Short-term clinical trials have confirmed that low-dose metformin (250 mg/day) suppresses formation of colorectal aberrant crypt foci, an early marker of colorectal carcinogenesis.
proposed: In one small randomized trial of nondiabetic patients with ACF, low-dose metformin (250 mg/d) was associated with a significant decrease in mean ACF number at 1 month, whereas it did not change significantly in the control group.
why: Narrowed from 'short-term trials have confirmed' to one randomized trial of 26 patients; dropped 'early marker of carcinogenesis', which no quote states. Quote 1 gives dose and design, quote 0 the result.

evidence.quote: At 1 month, the metformin group had a significant decrease in the mean number of ACF per patient (8.78 +/- 6.45 before treatment versus 5.11 +/- 4.99 at 1 month, P = 0.007), whereas the mean ACF number did not change significantly in the control group (7.23 +/- 6.65 versus 7.56 +/- 6.75, P = 0.609).

We prospectively randomized 26 nondiabetic patients with ACF to treatment with metformin (250 mg/d, n = 12) or no treatment (control, n = 14); 23 patients were evaluable for end point analyses (9 metformin and 14 control); the two groups were similar in ACF number and other baseline clinical characteristics.

original: COX-2 expression is virtually undetectable in normal intestinal mucosa but is markedly increased in approximately 50% of colonic adenomas and 90% of colorectal carcinomas.
proposed: COX-2 expression in adenoma tissue has been reported to be higher than in adjacent normal tissue, and high levels of COX-2 protein have been found in human and animal colorectal tumors.
why: Dropped 'virtually undetectable' normal mucosa and the 50% and 90% figures, which neither quote states. Quote 0 gives adenoma versus adjacent normal; quote 1 gives high COX-2 in colorectal tumors.

evidence.quote: The expression of COX-2 in the adenoma tissue was higher than that in the adjacent normal tissue in the patients with and without snow-white sign (P<0.001,P=0.004).
Investigation of the molecular basis of these observations showed that high levels of COX-2 protein were present in both human and animal colorectal tumors.

original: Direct effects on cancer cells involve activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), leading to inhibition of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway—a critical regulator of cell growth and metabolism frequently dysregulated in cancer.
proposed: Direct effects on cancer cells involve AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), which modulates mTOR signaling, leading to cell growth inhibition and cell cycle arrest.
why: Replaced 'activation of AMPK leading to inhibition of mTOR' with the quote's wording that AMPK modulates mTOR and Akt signaling, with growth inhibition and arrest; dropped the 'critical regulator' remark.

evidence.quote: AMPK is closely correlated to the tumor-suppressive functions of LKB1 and P53, consequently modulating the activity of cellular survival signaling such as mTOR and Akt, leading to cell growth inhibition and cell cycle arrest.

original: Exceptions exist: aspirin and tamoxifen show clear benefit when targeted to defined high-risk populations, though wider application remains problematic.
proposed: Tamoxifen shows clear benefit when targeted to a defined high-risk population: a major clinical trial in the United States found that it reduced the incidence of breast cancer by almost 50% in women at an increased risk for the disease.
why: Dropped aspirin and the 'wider application remains problematic' remark, which the quote does not cover. Kept tamoxifen's roughly 50% reduction in high-risk women.

evidence.quote: A major clinical trial in the United States found that tamoxifen reduced the incidence of breast cancer by almost 50% in women at an increased risk for the disease.

original: Fenretinide represents a leading candidate for bladder cancer chemoprevention, having demonstrated high therapeutic index in rodent models and encouraging results in phase IIa trials.
proposed: Fenretinide is being explored in ongoing clinical trials in patients with a history of superficial bladder cancer, and retinoids in general have been reported active against superficial bladder cancer in preclinical and clinical studies.
why: Dropped 'leading candidate', high therapeutic index in rodents and phase IIa results, none of which are stated. Quote 1 says fenretinide trials are ongoing; quote 0 gives retinoid activity in bladder cancer.

evidence.quote: Analyses of preclinical and clinical studies have shown retinoids to be active in reversing skin and oral precancer, in preventing primary skin cancer, superficial bladder cancer, and second primary tumours associated with head and neck and lung cancers.
Ongoing clinical trials are exploring the roles of fenretinide, difluoromethylornithine, and celecoxib in the treatment of patients with a history of superficial bladder cancer.

original: Indirect effects occur through systemic metabolic changes, including reduction of insulin and insulin-like growth factors, both of which have been implicated in cancer development and progression.
proposed: Insulin and insulin-like growth factors have been implicated in cancer development and progression: insulin and IGF-1 are described as growth factors that enhance tumor cell proliferation, and their effects on breast cancer development and progression have been shown in animal and human studies.
why: Dropped the indirect effect via systemic metabolic reduction of insulin and IGFs, which no quote states. Quote 0 gives proliferation; quote 1 gives breast cancer development and progression in animal and human studies.

evidence.quote: Recent evidence supports the role of insulin and IGF-1 as important growth factors, acting through the tyrosine kinase growth factor cascade in enhancing tumor cell proliferation.

Their effects on promoting breast cancer development, progression, and adverse outcomes have been demonstrated in both animal and human studies, suggesting that the IGF system is a potential target for breast cancer therapy.

original: Rationale and Mechanism: Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) has emerged as a compelling molecular target for cancer chemoprevention based on strong mechanistic rationale and epidemiological evidence.
proposed: Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) has been proposed as a molecular target for cancer chemoprevention, since epidemiological, clinical and experimental studies established NSAIDs as promising chemopreventive agents, and low-dose aspirin and NSAIDs inhibit COX-2, which has procarcinogenic effects.
why: Replaced 'has emerged as a compelling target' and 'strong' evidence with what the quotes state: evidence for NSAIDs as chemopreventive agents (quote 0) and COX-2 inhibition with procarcinogenic effects (quote 1).

evidence.quote: Several epidemiological, clinical and experimental studies established nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) as promising cancer chemopreventive agents.
Low-dose aspirin and NSAIDs are potential chemopreventive candidates because they inhibit the enzyme COX-2 which has a number of procarcinogenic effects.

original: Strikingly, two trials in smokers found that beta-carotene was associated with statistically significant increased incidence of lung cancer, directly contradicting epidemiological observations linking dietary beta-carotene intake with reduced lung cancer risk.
proposed: Strikingly, two trials found that beta-carotene was associated with a higher incidence of lung cancer: 18 percent higher among men in one, and 2.0% versus 0.9% in the other, mostly in former smokers.
why: Dropped 'in smokers', 'statistically significant' for both, and the contradiction with epidemiological observations, which no quote states. Quote 0 gives the 18% increase (CI 3 to 36%); quote 1 the second trial.

evidence.quote: Unexpectedly, we observed a higher incidence of lung cancer among the men who received beta carotene than among those who did not (change in incidence, 18 percent; 95 percent confidence interval, 3 to 36 percent).
More lung cancers were noted in the beta carotene vs no beta carotene group (23 [2.0%] vs 11 [0.9%], nominal P = .04), mostly in former smokers.

original: Tamoxifen increases risks of endometrial cancer and thromboembolic events; raloxifene carries thromboembolic risks.
proposed: Serious and life-threatening events with tamoxifen (SOLTAMOX) include uterine malignancies, stroke, and pulmonary embolism, and increased risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism has been reported with raloxifene.
why: Reworded to the label language: quote 0 lists uterine malignancies, stroke and pulmonary embolism for tamoxifen; quote 1 gives venous thromboembolism risk for raloxifene. Endometrial cancer by name and 'thromboembolic' for tamoxifen are not stated.

evidence.quote: Serious and life-threatening events from the use of SOLTAMOX include uterine malignancies, stroke, and pulmonary embolism
WARNING: INCREASED RISK OF VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM AND DEATH FROM STROKE Increased risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism have been reported with raloxifene hydrochloride

original: Synergistic Benefits Across Disease Categories: An important advantage of lifestyle-based prevention strategies is that they address risk factors common to multiple chronic diseases.
proposed: An advantage of lifestyle-based prevention strategies may be that they address risk factors, such as physical inactivity and poor diet, that are shared by several chronic diseases.
why: Softened a flat claim: quote 0 proposes lifestyle measures to prevent several chronic diseases, and quote 1 lists shared risk factors (inactivity, poor diet) promoting chronic inflammation. 'Synergistic' benefit is not stated.

evidence.quote: Evidence-based prevention for the diseases noted above include lifestyle management, cessation of smoking, curtailing excessive alcohol consumption, a healthy diet and moderate exercise, as well as mentally stimulating activities.

In the present Perspective we describe the multi-level mechanisms underlying SCI and several risk factors that promote this health-damaging phenotype, including infections, physical inactivity, poor diet, environmental and industrial toxicants and psychological stress.

original: Tamoxifen and raloxifene for breast cancer prevention represent successful examples in appropriately selected high-risk women, while the cardiovascular toxicity of COX-2 inhibitors illustrates how even demonstrated efficacy may be outweighed by toxicity concerns.
proposed: Tamoxifen and raloxifene for breast cancer prevention represent successful examples in appropriately selected high-risk women: together with two aromatase inhibitors, they reduced breast cancer incidence by 50%-65% in multiple randomized trials.
why: Dropped the COX-2 cardiovascular toxicity clause, which the quote does not mention. The 50%-65% reduction applies to the four agents together in high-risk women.

evidence.quote: In multiple randomized trials, two selective estrogen receptor modulators - tamoxifen and raloxifene, and two aromatase inhibitors - exemestane and anastrozole have reduced BC incidence by 50%-65% in high-risk women.

original: MCED tests are built upon the concept of liquid biopsy, which leverages the knowledge that blood and bodily secretions contain tumor-derived materials including circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, cellular components, and tumor metabolites.
proposed: Multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests rely on blood-based analysis of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) or cell-free DNA, and in one prospective study a cfDNA sequencing test with machine learning detected cancer signals across multiple cancer types.
why: Dropped the liquid-biopsy concept and the list of circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, components and metabolites, which the quotes do not name. Kept ctDNA/cfDNA as the analyte (quotes 0 and 1).

evidence.quote: Despite their promise, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based assays for multi-cancer early detection face challenges in test performance, due mostly to the limited abundance of ctDNA and its inherent variability.

The Circulating Cell-free Genome Atlas study (CCGA; NCT02889978) was a prospective, case-controlled, observational study and demonstrated that a blood-based MCED test utilizing cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing in combination with machine learning could detect cancer signals across multiple cancer types and predict cancer signal origin (CSO) with high accuracy.

original: Regular Pap testing enables detection of precancerous changes before symptoms develop and has substantially reduced cervical cancer mortality since its widespread adoption.
proposed: Cervical cancer screening has accompanied profound decreases in cancer incidence and mortality over the last half century in the United States, and a 50-75% decrease in cervical cancer mortality is mentioned for populations with many preventive screening programs.
why: Dropped Pap testing by name, detection of precancerous changes before symptoms, and 'since its widespread adoption'; the quotes speak of screening programs generally and give the 50-75% mortality decrease.

evidence.quote: In populations with many preventive screening programs, a decrease in cervical cancer mortality of 50-75% is mentioned over the past 50 years.
Cervical cancer screening in the United States has accompanied profound decreases in cancer incidence and mortality over the last half century.

original: Cell blocks enable immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, and molecular testing previously reserved for histological specimens.
proposed: Cell blocks yield tissue sections that can be used for ancillary testing such as immunohistochemical stains and molecular studies.
why: Dropped in situ hybridization and 'previously reserved for histological specimens', which the quote does not state.

evidence.quote: In addition to serving as an adjunct to other cytologic preparations for morphologic diagnosis, cell blocks play an increasingly important role as they yield tissue sections that can be utilized for ancillary testing such as immunohistochemical stains and molecular studies.

original: The revised FIGO staging system markedly clarified tumor characteristics for each stage and incorporated molecular analysis data from the Cancer Genome Atlas, which are correlated with prognosis and treatment planning.
proposed: Recent updates to the FIGO staging system incorporate molecular features, allowing for more tailored treatment approaches, and TCGA data have provided improved clarity on the diverse biology of endometrial cancers and their differing prognostic outcomes.
why: Dropped 'markedly clarified tumor characteristics for each stage' and a direct link of TCGA data to the staging revision, which no quote states. Quote 1 gives molecular features and tailored treatment; quote 0 gives TCGA clarity.

evidence.quote: Molecular and genetic findings have accelerated since the publication of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data and provide improved clarity on the diverse biological nature of this collection of endometrial cancers and their differing prognostic outcomes.
Recent updates to the FIGO staging system incorporate molecular features, allowing for more tailored treatment approaches.

module: 2.1 Defining Cancer: Uncontrolled Growth and Invasion
original: Adrenal metastasis can occur from primaries in the lung (39%), breast (35%), melanoma, gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, and kidney, among other places.
proposed: Adrenal metastasis can occur from primaries in the lung, renal cell, melanoma, sarcoma, colorectal, and hepatobiliary or gastrointestinal tract; in one series lung accounted for 47% and in another for 29%.
why: Dropped breast (35%), pancreas and the 39% lung figure, which the quotes do not support. The quotes give lung 47% and 29%, with renal cell, melanoma, sarcoma, colorectal and GI/hepatobiliary primaries.

evidence.quote: The most common primary malignancies were lung (n = 125, 47%), renal cell (n = 38, 14%), melanoma (n = 33, 12%), sarcoma (n = 18, 7%), and colorectal (n = 12, 5%).
Metastatic carcinomas included lung (n = 21 of 72, 29%), genitourinary (n = 12 of 72, 17%), and hepatobiliary or gastrointestinal tract (n = 11 of 72, 15%) primaries.

module: 2.1 Defining Cancer: Uncontrolled Growth and Invasion
original: The cancerous cell is particularly characterized by a poor use of oxygen and the massive use of glucose, which is exclusively converted to lactic acid.
proposed: The cancerous cell is particularly characterized by increased glucose uptake, with most of the glucose fermented to lactate even in the presence of oxygen and fully functioning mitochondria (the Warburg effect).
why: Replaced 'poor use of oxygen' and 'exclusively converted' with the quotes' wording: increased uptake and fermentation of the majority of glucose to lactate in oxygenated tumors, even with functioning mitochondria.

evidence.quote: The common feature of this altered metabolism is the increased glucose uptake and fermentation of glucose to lactate. This phenomenon is observed even in the presence of completely functioning mitochondria and, together, is known as the 'Warburg Effect'.

A long-standing question in cancer biology has been why oxygenated tumors ferment the majority of glucose they consume to lactate rather than oxidizing it in their mitochondria, a phenomenon known as the 'Warburg effect.'

module: 2.1 Defining Cancer: Uncontrolled Growth and Invasion
original: The median time from cancer diagnosis to the identification of adrenal metastases is about 2.5 years, although adrenal metastases have been reported up to 22 years after initial treatment of primary tumors.
proposed: In one series, the median time to detection of adrenal metastasis after initial diagnosis of the primary tumor was 17 months (interquartile range 6-41), and in a lung cancer cohort the median time to detection of the metastasis was 11 months.
why: Replaced the 2.5-year median and the 22-year maximum, which no quote supports, with the medians the quotes report: 17 months and 11 months.

evidence.quote: The median time to detection of adrenal metastasis after initial diagnosis of the primary tumor was 17 months (interquartile range: 6-41).
Median time to detection of the metastasis was 11 months, and 41.8% were ipsilateral to the primary lung cancer.

original: Virchow was the first to correctly link the origin of cancers from otherwise normal cells, believing that cancer is caused by severe irritation in the tissues (the 'chronic irritation theory').
proposed: Virchow proposed the 'chronic irritation theory', that cancer is caused by irritation in the tissues, and this theory engendered the essential role of inflammation in carcinogenesis.
why: Dropped 'first to correctly link the origin of cancers from normal cells' and 'severe', which no quote states. Quote 0 gives the irritation theory and inflammation; quote 1 attributes the irritation theory to Virchow.

evidence.quote: Virchow's irritation theory based on human cancer engendered the essential role of inflammation in carcinogenesis.
His greatest error was his rejection of the theory of irritation promulgated by his teacher Virchow.

original: Hanahan and Weinberg identified these traits as the hallmarks of cancer, which include increased cell proliferation, achieved through sustained proliferative signaling or evasion of growth suppressors.
proposed: The hallmarks of cancer include sustaining proliferative signaling and evading growth suppressors, along with resisting cell death, enabling replicative immortality, inducing angiogenesis, and activating invasion and metastasis.
why: The quote lists the hallmarks but does not name Hanahan and Weinberg or say proliferation is 'achieved through' the two traits, so both were dropped and the quote's list used.

evidence.quote: They include sustaining proliferative signaling, evading growth suppressors, resisting cell death, enabling replicative immortality, inducing angiogenesis, and activating invasion and metastasis.

original: The enabling characteristic identified in 2000 as "genomic instability" was described in 2011 as "genomic instability and mutation", and a second enabling characteristic was identified as "tumor-promoting inflammation".
proposed: The enabling characteristics underlying the hallmarks are genome instability, which generates the genetic diversity that expedites their acquisition, and inflammation, which fosters multiple hallmark functions.
why: Dropped the 2000 versus 2011 naming history and the quoted labels, which the quote does not state. Kept genome instability and inflammation as underlying characteristics.

evidence.quote: Underlying these hallmarks are genome instability, which generates the genetic diversity that expedites their acquisition, and inflammation, which fosters multiple hallmark functions.

original: The identification of "tumour-promoting inflammation" as the second enabling characteristic recognizes that inflammation causes the emergence of several of the hallmarks, including sustaining proliferative signalling and inducing angiogenesis.
proposed: Inflammation, one of the characteristics underlying the hallmarks, fosters multiple hallmark functions; for example, IL-6 is high in the tumour microenvironment and promotes tumorigenesis by regulating hallmarks including proliferation and angiogenesis.
why: Replaced 'causes the emergence of' with 'fosters' (quote 0); dropped the 'second enabling characteristic' naming. Quote 1 adds IL-6 regulating proliferation and angiogenesis.

evidence.quote: Underlying these hallmarks are genome instability, which generates the genetic diversity that expedites their acquisition, and inflammation, which fosters multiple hallmark functions.

The strong association between inflammation and cancer is reflected by the high IL-6 levels in the tumour microenvironment, where it promotes tumorigenesis by regulating all hallmarks of cancer and multiple signalling pathways, including apoptosis, survival, proliferation, angiogenesis, invasiveness and metastasis, and, most importantly, the metabolism.

original: Angiosarcoma (AS) comprises 1% of all soft-tissue sarcoma (STS), which are themselves a rare malignancy.
proposed: Angiosarcoma (AS) is a rare tumor accounting for 1-2% of all soft-tissue sarcoma (STS).
why: Replaced '1%' with the quote's 1-2% and dropped the statement that STS are themselves rare, which the quote does not make.

evidence.quote: Angiosarcomas are rare tumors accounting for 1-2% of all soft tissue sarcomas.

original: Local recurrences can occur in all phyllodes tumors at an overall rate of 21%, with ranges of 10% to 17%, 14% to 25%, and 23% to 30% for benign, borderline malignant, and phyllodes tumors, respectively.
proposed: Local recurrences can occur in phyllodes tumors, with pooled estimated recurrence rates of 7.1%, 16.7%, and 25.1% for benign, borderline, and malignant tumors, respectively.
why: Replaced the 21% overall rate and the ranges with the pooled rates in quote 0. Quote 1 gives 21-36% recurrence in an unspecified setting and was not used.

evidence.quote: The pooled estimated recurrence rates of benign, borderline, and malignant tumors were 7.1%, 16.7%, and 25.1%, respectively.

original: About one-quarter of cancers in low- and middle-income nations are due to infections such as Helicobacter pylori, which can cause stomach cancer; HPV, which can cause cervical, anal, throat, and penile cancer; and the hepatitis B and C viruses, which can cause liver cancer.
proposed: An estimated 21% of cancer cases in developing countries (about 1,000,000 fewer cases per year), and 9% in developed countries, would not occur if the infectious diseases involved were prevented.
why: Changed 'about one-quarter in low- and middle-income nations' to the quote's 21% for developing countries and 9% for developed countries; dropped the named pathogens and cancers, which the quote does not list.

evidence.quote: There would be 21% fewer cases of cancer in developing countries (1,000,000 fewer cases per year) and 9% fewer cases in developed countries (375,000 fewer cases per year) if these infectious diseases were prevented.

original: Chronic HEPATITIS B VIRUS (HBV) infection (chronic hepatitis) causes about 52% of the world's hepatocellular carcinomas, resulting in nearly 340,000 deaths per year.
proposed: It is estimated that more than 50% of liver cancers worldwide are attributable to hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, and up to 89% of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma cases are from developing countries.
why: Replaced 'about 52%' and the '340,000 deaths per year' figure, which the quote does not give, with 'more than 50%' of liver cancers and the 89% developing-country share.

evidence.quote: It is estimated that more than 50% of liver cancers worldwide are attributable to HBV and up to 89% of HBV-related HCC are from developing countries.

original: Massetti emphasized that almost a third of cancer deaths globally are due to leading preventable risk factors like obesity, lack of physical activity, tobacco use, and alcohol use.
proposed: One review argued that between a third and a half of cancers are preventable on the basis of present knowledge of risk factors.
why: Dropped the attribution to Massetti and the 'almost a third of cancer deaths' figure; the quote speaks of a third to a half of cancers being preventable, not deaths, and names no specific risk factors.

evidence.quote: We argue that primary prevention is a particularly effective way to fight cancer, with between a third and a half of cancers being preventable on the basis of present knowledge of risk factors.

original: Massetti stressed that 30 percent of cancer deaths globally are due to leading preventable risk factors such as obesity, lack of physical activity, tobacco and alcohol use, exposure to radiation and other carcinogens, and some infections.
proposed: One review argues that primary prevention is a particularly effective way to fight cancer, with between a third and a half of cancers being preventable on the basis of present knowledge of risk factors.
why: Dropped Massetti, the 30 percent of cancer deaths figure and the named risk factors; the quote gives a third to a half of cancers as preventable and does not mention deaths or the listed exposures.

evidence.quote: We argue that primary prevention is a particularly effective way to fight cancer, with between a third and a half of cancers being preventable on the basis of present knowledge of risk factors.

original: More than 90% of cancers are directly attributable to environmental and lifestyle factors, making them largely preventable.
proposed: Most colorectal cancers are sporadic and largely attributable to modifiable environmental risk factors such as obesity, physical inactivity, poor diet, alcohol drinking and smoking, although another analysis suggests that only a third of the variation in cancer risk among tissues is attributable to environmental factors or inherited predispositions.
why: Replaced 'more than 90% of cancers' with the colorectal cancer majority in quote 0, and added quote 1's one-third figure so the claim is not left contradicted. 'Largely preventable' is not stated.

evidence.quote: Yet, the majority of CRC is sporadic and largely attributable to the constellation of modifiable environmental risk factors characterizing westernization (for example, obesity, physical inactivity, poor diets, alcohol drinking and smoking).
These results suggest that only a third of the variation in cancer risk among tissues is attributable to environmental factors or inherited predispositions.

original: Nearly half of cancers—42 percent—are attributed to modifiable risk factors.
proposed: In the United States in 2019, an estimated 40.0% of incident cancers and 44.0% of cancer deaths in adults aged 30 years and older were attributable to the evaluated risk factors.
why: Replaced 'nearly half, 42 percent' (the 2014 figure) with the 2019 values of 40.0% and 44.0%, and 'modifiable risk factors' with 'the evaluated risk factors' as quoted.

evidence.quote: In 2019, an estimated 40.0% (713,340 of 1,781,649) of all incident cancers (excluding nonmelanoma skin cancers) and 44.0% (262,120 of 595,737) of all cancer deaths in adults aged 30 years and older in the United States were attributable to the evaluated risk factors.

original: There is convincing epidemiological evidence from both cohort and case-control studies that alcohol consumption increases the risk of cancers of the mouth, pharynx, larynx, and esophagus.
proposed: There is epidemiological evidence that alcohol increases the risk of cancers of the oral cavity and pharynx, larynx, and oesophagus, as well as colorectum, liver and female breast, with a clear dose-risk relationship.
why: Dropped 'cohort and case-control studies', which the quotes do not name. Widened the site list to what quote 0 concludes (adding colorectum, liver and female breast) and added the dose-risk relationship from quote 1.

evidence.quote: CONCLUSIONS: Alcohol increases risk of cancer of oral cavity and pharynx, oesophagus, colorectum, liver, larynx and female breast.

Relative risks (RRs) for heavy drinkers compared with nondrinkers and occasional drinkers were 5.13 for oral and pharyngeal cancer, 4.95 for oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma, 1.44 for colorectal, 2.65 for laryngeal and 1.61 for breast cancer; for those neoplasms there was a clear dose-risk relationship.

original: TOBACCO, through its various forms of exposure, constitutes the main cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide among men, and increasingly among women.
proposed: Smoking was the leading risk factor for risk-attributable cancer deaths globally in 2019 for both sexes combined, followed by alcohol use and high BMI.
why: Narrowed to the quote's finding: global 2019 data, both sexes combined. Dropped 'among men, and increasingly among women', which is not stated, and the 'main cause' wording.

evidence.quote: The leading risk factors at the most detailed level globally for risk-attributable cancer deaths and DALYs in 2019 for both sexes combined were smoking, followed by alcohol use and high BMI.

original: Ultraviolet radiation is a recognized cause of skin cancer including malignant melanomas.
proposed: Ultraviolet radiation exposure increases an individual's risk of cutaneous carcinogenesis, and 60 to 70 percent of melanomas are thought to be caused by ultraviolet radiation.
why: Replaced 'recognized cause' with the quotes' hedged wording: 60-70% of melanomas are 'thought to be caused' by UV, and UV increases the risk of cutaneous carcinogenesis.

evidence.quote: Sixty to seventy percent of melanomas are thought to be caused by ultraviolet radiation.
Ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure, which increases an individual's risk of cutaneous carcinogenesis, may be a particularly significant risk factor when it occurs during childhood.

original: The complete surgical cytoreduction possible is decisive for the prognosis, which requires multiple organ resections in addition to a partial to subtotal parietal peritonectomy.
proposed: A complete cytoreduction is decisive for the prognosis, which in most cases requires multi-organ resection in addition to a partial or subtotal parietal peritonectomy.
why: The quote says 'in most cases', so the flat statement that multiple organ resections are required was hedged to match it.

evidence.quote: Decisive for the prognosis is a complete cytoreduction, which in most cases necessitates multi-organ resection in addition to a partial or subtotal parietal peritonectomy (PE).

original: The move towards extensive surgery has been coupled with a greater stringency as to what constitutes optimal cytoreduction; this is increasingly being defined as removal of all macroscopic disease.
proposed: In one study, maximal debulking was defined as no gross residual tumor, while optimal and suboptimal debulking were used for patients with residual tumors of 1 cm or less and more than 1 cm, respectively; complete macroscopic resection in ovarian cancer is associated with improved survival.
why: Dropped the claim that optimal cytoreduction is increasingly defined as removing all macroscopic disease; quote 0 defines optimal as residual of 1 cm or less and maximal as none. Kept quote 1's survival association.

evidence.quote: Maximal debulking was defined as no gross residual tumor after primary or recurrence surgery; optimal and suboptimal debulking were used for patients with residual tumors of ≤1cm and >1cm, respectively.
Cytoreductive surgery with complete macroscopic resection in patients with ovarian cancer is associated with improved survival.

original: To quantify the extent of peritoneal metastases and determine the feasibility of tumor reduction, a surgical variable is used (index of peritoneal carcinomatosis: PCI).
proposed: To quantify tumour burden in peritoneal metastases and help select patients, the peritoneal carcinomatosis index (PCI) is used.
why: Replaced 'determine the feasibility of tumor reduction' and 'surgical variable' with what the quotes state: PCI quantifies tumour burden and is used in patient selection and in assessing criteria for unresectability.

evidence.quote: It is important to have an awareness of the different forms of presentation, methods of quantifying tumour burden (peritoneal carcinomatosis index, PCI), and criteria for unresectability for an accurate assessment of the disease's status.

It is also vital for appropriate patient selection, using the acronym "PAUSE", which involves assessing tumor burden via the peritoneal carcinomatosis index, evaluating patients pre- and post-therapy, detecting complications following therapy, and predicting treatment outcomes.

original: True colonic mucosal recurrences are rare.
proposed: In one study, anastomotic recurrences were rare, and the majority were in patients who had rectal cancer.
why: Narrowed 'true colonic mucosal recurrences' to the quote's anastomotic recurrences and added that most were in rectal cancer patients.

evidence.quote: Anastomotic recurrences were rare, and the majority were in patients who had rectal cancer that could be evaluated by in-office flexible sigmoidoscopy.

original: Evidence of moderate quality supports that robotic surgery for rectal cancer is a valid alternative and complementary approach with beneficial effects, particularly in centers with expertise in minimally invasive techniques.
proposed: Robot-assisted surgery for rectal cancer has become more popular despite seemingly weak evidence of clinical benefit, and recently published high-quality studies show advantages for robotic resection; however, in one trial it did not significantly reduce the risk of conversion to open laparotomy compared with conventional laparoscopic surgery.
why: Dropped 'moderate quality' and 'centers with expertise', which no quote states. Quote 0 gives the weak earlier evidence and newer reported advantages; quote 1 tempers it with a null result on conversion to open surgery.

evidence.quote: In this respect robot-assisted surgery has become more and more popular despite seemingly weak evidence regarding clinical benefits and the not to be ignored economic aspects; however, recently published high-quality studies provide new evidence showing advantages for a robotic resection in patients suffering from rectal cancer.

Among patients with rectal adenocarcinoma suitable for curative resection, robotic-assisted laparoscopic surgery, as compared with conventional laparoscopic surgery, did not significantly reduce the risk of conversion to open laparotomy.

original: Adipose tissue undergoes decellularization using physical, chemical, and enzymatic methods, followed by disinfection steps, creating a bioink that can be loaded with human adipose-derived stem cells (hASCs) and printed into patient-specific shapes.
proposed: In one study, a bioink made from decellularized adipose tissue (DAT) matrix encapsulating human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hASCs) was used to print adipose tissue constructs, and direct printing of customized tissue analogs is described as a promising approach to soft tissue regeneration.
why: Dropped the decellularization methods (physical, chemical, enzymatic), disinfection steps and 'patient-specific shapes', which the quotes do not describe. Kept the DAT bioink with hASCs and the promising-approach statement.

evidence.quote: Here, we devise a biomimetic approach for printing adipose tissue constructs employing decellularized adipose tissue (DAT) matrix bioink encapsulating human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hASCs).
This study demonstrates that direct printing of spatially on-demand customized tissue analogs is a promising approach to soft tissue regeneration.

original: The essential differences between oncoplastic surgery and conventional breast-conserving surgery include capacity for larger volume excisions, reduced re-excision rates, and decreased rates of positive margins.
proposed: Oncoplastic surgery has emerged as a new approach for extending the possibilities of breast-conserving surgery, reducing both mastectomy and re-excision rates while avoiding breast deformities.
why: Dropped 'larger volume excisions' and 'decreased rates of positive margins', which the quote does not state. Kept the reduced re-excision rate and added the quote's reduced mastectomy rate and avoidance of deformities.

evidence.quote: Oncoplastic surgery (OPS) has emerged as a new approach for extending breast conserving surgery (BCS) possibilities, reducing both mastectomy and re-excision rates, while avoiding breast deformities.

module: 21.1 Principles of Radiotherapy: Biological Effects on Cells
original: The importance of DNA repair is illustrated by diseases such as ataxia-telangiectasia (AT), where defects in the ATM protein lead to hypersensitivity to ionizing radiation and increased cancer risk.
proposed: Mutations in the ATM gene are associated with ataxia-telangiectasia (AT), an autosomal recessive disorder.
why: Dropped DNA repair importance, hypersensitivity to ionizing radiation and increased cancer risk, which the quote does not state. It only links gene mutations to ataxia telangiectasia as an autosomal recessive disorder.

evidence.quote: Mutations in this gene are associated with ataxia telangiectasia, an autosomal recessive disorder.

module: 21.1 Principles of Radiotherapy: Biological Effects on Cells
original: The p53 tumor suppressor protein plays a crucial role in radiation-induced apoptosis, though p53-independent pathways involving Bcl-2/BAX also contribute.
proposed: p53 plays a role in radiation-induced apoptosis: p53-dependent up-regulation of the pro-apoptotic Bcl2 family molecules PUMA, Noxa, and Bim leads to mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and caspase-dependent apoptosis, and in mice gamma-irradiation induced p53-dependent ARTS expression.
why: Dropped the p53-independent Bcl-2/BAX contribution, which neither quote addresses. Quote 0 gives the p53-dependent Bcl2-family pathway; quote 1 gives p53-dependent ARTS induction by gamma-irradiation in mice.

evidence.quote: This is followed by the p53-dependent up-regulation of the pro-apoptotic Bcl2 family molecules, including the BH3-only molecules PUMA, Noxa, and Bim, leading to mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) and the release of cytochrome c, which activates caspase-dependent apoptosis.
Also, γ-irradiation induced p53-dependent ARTS expression in mice.

original: Carbon ions create a unique DNA damage signature characterized by complex clustered lesions that overwhelm DNA repair capacity of malignant cells.
proposed: Heavy ions produce dense ionization along their trajectories and cause irreparable clustered DNA damage, and carbon ion irradiation may overcome radioresistance by inducing more complex DNA damage and apoptosis.
why: Replaced the flat statement about a 'unique signature' that 'overwhelms repair capacity' with the quotes' wording: irreparable clustered damage from heavy ions, and carbon ions 'may' overcome radioresistance.

evidence.quote: Immediately after irradiation, heavy ions produce dense ionization along their trajectories, cause irreparable clustered DNA damage, and alter cellular ultrastructure.

These results suggest that carbon ion irradiation may overcome radioresistance by inducing more complex DNA damage and apoptosis, thus providing insights for targeting new strategies in combining gene therapy with radiotherapy.

original: Following thyroidectomy for differentiated thyroid cancers (papillary, follicular), I-131 ablates remnant thyroid tissue and treats metastatic disease, improving disease-free survival and overall survival in intermediate and high-risk patients.
proposed: Recurrence and distant metastasis of follicular thyroid cancer (FTC) are treated with radioactive iodine (RAI).
why: Dropped the thyroidectomy setting, remnant ablation, papillary cancer and any survival benefit in intermediate and high-risk patients; the quote only says RAI treats recurrence and distant metastasis of FTC.

evidence.quote: Recurrence and distant metastasis of FTC are treated with radioactive iodine (RAI).

original: For endometrial cancer vaginal cuff boost, advanced EBRT planning techniques using IMRT or volumetric modulated arc therapy can create brachytherapy-like dose distributions when brachytherapy is not feasible.
proposed: For vaginal cuff boost, advanced EBRT techniques such as IMRT and VMAT are capable of making plans that closely resemble HDR-VCBT plans.
why: Dropped 'endometrial cancer' and 'when brachytherapy is not feasible', which the quote does not state; the quote says IMRT and VMAT can make plans that closely resemble HDR-VCBT.

evidence.quote: Advanced EBRT techniques such as IMRT and VMAT are capable of making plans, which closely resemble HDR-VCBT.

original: Intensity modulation has permitted radiation oncologists to place sharper dose gradients across normal tissue structures (including bladder, rectum, salivary glands, and spinal cord) with increased dose to tumor targets, allowing higher doses with no additional clinical morbidity.
proposed: Intensity modulation (IMRT) allows conformal dose distributions around a tumor target with a rapid dose fall-off that spares surrounding critical structures, which is particularly suited to head and neck cancers because it allows potential dose escalation; in one study of locally advanced pancreatic cancer, hypofractionated full-dose gemcitabine IMRT improved overall survival without increased GI toxicities compared with conventionally fractionated low-dose gemcitabine 3DCRT.
why: Dropped the named organs and 'no additional clinical morbidity' in general. Quote 0 gives sparing of critical structures and potential dose escalation in head and neck; quote 1 gives one pancreatic cancer comparison.

evidence.quote: This technology allows for conformal dose distributions around a tumor target while a rapid dose fall-off spares surrounding critical structures. The properties of IMRT are particularly suited for treating head and neck cancers due to the close proximity of dose-limiting normal tissues allowing for potential dose escalation.

LAPC patients treated with hypofractionated full-dose gemcitabine IMRT had improved OS and LRPFS without increased GI toxicities when compared to those of patients treated with conventionally fractionated low dose gemcitabine 3DCRT.

original: Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) using lutetium-177 (Lu-177) conjugated to somatostatin analogs (Lu-177 DOTATATE) targets somatostatin receptors overexpressed on neuroendocrine tumors, providing both symptomatic control and survival benefit in progressive metastatic disease.
proposed: Lutetium Lu 177 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors with highest affinity for subtype 2 (SSTR2), and the radiolabeled somatostatin analog LUTATHERA is indicated for adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs).
why: Dropped 'overexpressed', 'symptomatic control and survival benefit' and 'progressive metastatic disease', which no quote states. Quote 0 gives receptor binding; quote 1 gives the indicated population.

evidence.quote: Lutetium Lu 177 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors with highest affinity for subtype 2 somatostatin receptors (SSTR2).

LUTATHERA is a radiolabeled somatostatin analog indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs), including foregut, midgut, and hindgut neuroendocrine tumors.

original: Radiation emitted from targeted cells can penetrate and destroy adjacent tumor cells even if they lack the tumor-associated antigen or receptor, potentially overcoming tumor heterogeneity where not all malignant cells express the target.
proposed: In a spheroid model, 177Lu cross-fire enabled full dose coverage even when the radiopharmaceutical had accumulated in only 60% of the cells, and radioimmunotherapy has been described as able to target antigen-negative leukemic stem cells.
why: Narrowed 'tumor cells generally' to what the quotes cover: a spheroid model with 177Lu (quote 1) and antigen-negative leukemic stem cells (quote 0). Dropped the heterogeneity inference and 'destroy adjacent tumor cells'.

evidence.quote: Its ability to target antigen negative LSC gives it an advantage compared with other forms of immunotherapy.
We observed that for 177Lu, radiation cross-fire enabled full dose coverage even if the radiopharmaceutical had accumulated to only 60% of the spheroid cells.

original: Randomized trials comparing proton versus carbon ion therapy for skull base chondrosarcomas and chordomas are ongoing to definitively establish comparative effectiveness.
proposed: Phase III randomised trials comparing proton with carbon ion radiation therapy have been registered for patients with low and intermediate grade chondrosarcoma of the skull base and for patients with chordoma of the skull base.
why: The quotes are trial titles only; 'are ongoing' and 'to definitively establish comparative effectiveness' are not stated, so the sentence says only that the randomised trials exist.

evidence.quote: Randomised Trial of Proton vs. Carbon Ion Radiation Therapy in Patients With Low and Inter-mediate Grade Chondrosarcoma of the Skull Base, Clinical Phase III Study
Randomised Trial of Proton vs. Carbon Ion Radiation Therapy in Patients With Chordoma of the Skull Base -Clinical Phase III Study-

original: The inability to deliver adequate brachytherapy boost is associated with inferior survival outcomes.
proposed: In selected patients with glioblastoma, combining full-dose external beam radiotherapy with a brachytherapy or radiosurgery boost leads to an increase in median survival whereas external beam radiation alone does not, although in a trial of dose-escalated EBRT no significant overall survival difference was observed between the treatment arms.
