why: Replaced the general claim about inferior survival when a boost cannot be delivered with the glioblastoma finding (quote 0) and added the contrary no-survival-difference finding from quote 1.

evidence.quote: Combination of full-dose external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy or radiosurgery boost in selected patients with glioblastoma leads to an increase in the median survival, while external beam radiation alone in patients with similar prognosis does not.

Although biochemical failure was associated with increased mortality and randomization to DE-EBRT doubled the rate of biochemical failure, no significant overall survival difference was observed between the treatment arms (MVA HR 1.13; P=.62).

original: The relative biological effectiveness (RBE) of protons is approximately 1.1 compared to conventional photon therapy—meaning protons are slightly more effective biologically than photons at the same physical dose.
proposed: The relative biological effectiveness (RBE) of protons is simplistically assumed to have a constant value of 1.1, but in reality the RBE is variable and a complex function of the energy of protons, dose per fraction, tissue and cell type, end point, and other factors.
why: The quote says 1.1 is a simplistic assumption and that the true RBE varies, so the flat statement of approximately 1.1 was hedged. Dropped the 'slightly more effective than photons' gloss, which is not stated.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the relative biological effectiveness (RBE) of protons is simplistically assumed to have a constant value of 1.1. In reality, the RBE is variable and a complex function of the energy of protons, dose per fraction, tissue and cell type, end point, etc.

original: A more recent development in MRI-guided RT is application of AI methods for automatic structure identification and segmentation in treatment planning.
proposed: Artificial intelligence methods are being applied in image-guided radiotherapy, including auto-segmentation on IGRT imaging, and machine learning methods have been extensively employed for mpMRI image classification, segmentation, registration and detection.
why: Dropped 'more recent development' and 'treatment planning', which the quotes do not state, and widened MRI-guided RT to the quotes' image-guided and mpMRI settings.

evidence.quote: In this review article, after outlining modern IGRT and online ART workflows, we cover the role of AI in CBCT and MRI correction for dose calculation, auto-segmentation on IGRT imaging, motion management, and response assessment based on in-room imaging.

Machine learning-based artificial intelligence (AI) methods, especially those adopting the deep learning technique, have been extensively employed to perform mpMRI image classification, segmentation, registration, detection, reconstruction, and super-resolution.

original: High-accuracy offline MRI planning requires addressing geometric distortions from hardware imperfections (gradient nonlinearities, magnetic field inhomogeneities, eddy currents) which are measured by manufacturers and corrected with image processing algorithms.
proposed: Geometric distortion in MRI arises mainly from gradient nonlinearity, static magnetic field (B0) inhomogeneity, and susceptibility effects, and vendor-provided distortion correction, 3D distortion mapping, and periodic quality assurance can reduce it to clinically acceptable levels, although standardized evaluation protocols remain limited.
why: Replaced 'eddy currents' and 'offline MRI planning requires' with the sources quote 0 lists (including susceptibility effects) and the mitigation steps from quote 1, with its caveat about limited standardization.

evidence.quote: Geometric distortion arises mainly from gradient nonlinearity, static magnetic field (B₀) inhomogeneity, and susceptibility effects, and tends to increase toward the periphery of the field of view.

Vendor-provided distortion correction, 3D distortion mapping, and periodic quality assurance (QA) can reduce distortion to clinically acceptable levels, although standardized evaluation protocols and cross-platform comparability remain limited.

original: Widespread implementation of adaptive radiotherapy, including MR-guided approaches, is only possible with AI automation to reduce on-table time to reasonable durations (currently 30-70 minutes per fraction).
proposed: Online adaptation currently takes approximately 45 minutes, during which intrafractional movements remain unaccounted for, and in one MRgRT study the average fraction duration was 45 minutes.
why: Dropped the claim that AI automation is required for widespread implementation, and the 30-70 minute range, which no quote states. The quotes give about 45 minutes per fraction.

evidence.quote: However, the process of online adaptation currently takes approximately 45 min during which intrafractional movements remain unaccounted for.
All patients completed MRgRT with an average fraction duration of 45 min.

original: Chronic effects include chronic diarrhea, malabsorption, recurrent bouts of ileus or obstruction, and proliferative mucosal telangiectasias or ulceration.
proposed: Late toxicities reported include fecal incontinence (up to 44%), diarrhea (up to 26.7%), and ulceration (up to 22.6%), and about one in five patients treated by radiation therapy will present clinical signs of radiation enteritis, including obstruction and malabsorption.
why: Dropped ileus and telangiectasias, which the quotes do not mention. Quote 1 gives the late toxicities with frequencies; quote 0 gives radiation enteritis signs including obstruction and malabsorption.

evidence.quote: Approximately one out of five patients treated by radiation therapy will present clinical signs of radiation enteritis, including obstruction, malabsorption, malnutrition and/or other complications.
The most commonly reported late toxicities were fecal incontinence (up to 44%), diarrhea (up to 26.7%), and ulceration (up to 22.6%).

original: Irradiation to ovaries leads to infertility or premature ovarian failure even at low doses, with increased sensitivity with advancing age.
proposed: Irradiation to ovaries has been associated with greater damage at higher doses and with older age at treatment.
why: Dropped infertility/premature failure and the low-dose claim, which the quote does not state; kept only the dose and age association. The quote says 'damage' without naming the ovaries.

evidence.quote: Higher doses and older age at treatment are both associated with greater damage.

original: Late complications include alopecia, telangiectasia, fibrosis of masticator muscles resulting in trismus in 5-10% of patients, alterations in taste sensations, and dysphagia.
proposed: In one study, 28.1% of patients without trismus before radiotherapy developed trismus for the first time at six months after radiotherapy.
why: Dropped the list of late complications and the 5-10% figure; the only quote reports 28.1% new trismus at six months and does not name fibrosis.

evidence.quote: At six months after radiotherapy, 28.1% of the patients without trismus prior to radiotherapy developed trismus for the first time.

original: AI automated planning tools like the Radiation Planning Assistant (RPA) aim to increase global access to radiation therapy by reducing dependence on scarce expert planners.
proposed: The Radiation Planning Assistant (RPA) is a web-based tool designed to improve access to high-quality radiation therapy in low-resource settings.
why: Dropped the AI automation and scarce-planner claims, which the quote does not mention; kept the stated aim of improving access in low-resource settings.

evidence.quote: The RPA, a web-based tool designed to improve access to high-quality RT in low-resource settings, has high rates of clinical acceptability by practicing clinicians around the world.

original: Cancer is projected to become the number one cause of death across the globe in the next 20 years, and the evidence demonstrates that more than 40 percent of patients with cancer would benefit from RT.
proposed: The best available evidence indicates that external beam radiotherapy is indicated in about 52% of patients with cancer, which is more than 40 percent.
why: Dropped the projection about cancer becoming the leading cause of death; the quote gives a calculated 52% with an evidence-based indication for external beam radiotherapy, not 'would benefit'.

evidence.quote: The proportion of patients with cancer in whom external beam radiotherapy is indicated according to the best available evidence was calculated to be 52%.

original: The barriers to RT implementation are numerous, including perceptions that it is expensive, complex, and unlikely to succeed due to shortage of qualified personnel and funding.
proposed: The barriers to RT implementation are numerous; the availability of a suitably trained workforce has been highlighted as a major limiting factor, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), and there are geographic and economic barriers to providing brachytherapy there.
why: Dropped the perceptions of cost, complexity and failure, which no quote states. Workforce shortage is named as a major limiting factor, and brachytherapy has geographic and economic barriers in LMICs.

evidence.quote: The availability of a suitably trained and credentialled workforce has also been highlighted as a major limiting factor to effective implementation of radiotherapy, particularly in LMICs.
However, there are numerous geographic and economic barriers to providing brachytherapy to cancer patients in LMICs.

original: The barriers to the implementation of RT are numerous and include perceptions that it is expensive, complex, and unlikely to succeed because of the shortage of qualified personnel and funding.
proposed: The barriers to the implementation of RT are numerous; the availability of a suitably trained workforce has been highlighted as a major limiting factor, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), and there are geographic and economic barriers to providing brachytherapy there.
why: Dropped the perceptions of cost, complexity and failure, which no quote states. Workforce shortage is named as a major limiting factor, and brachytherapy has geographic and economic barriers in LMICs.

evidence.quote: The availability of a suitably trained and credentialled workforce has also been highlighted as a major limiting factor to effective implementation of radiotherapy, particularly in LMICs.
However, there are numerous geographic and economic barriers to providing brachytherapy to cancer patients in LMICs.

module: 22.1 Principles of Chemotherapy: Mechanism of Action
original: Cancer cells acquire spontaneous mutations that cause drug resistance.
proposed: Cancer cells can acquire new mutations within the drug target: approximately 60% of patients with acquired resistance to the EGFR TKIs (erlotinib, gefitinib, and afatinib) develop a new mutation within the drug target.
why: Dropped 'spontaneous' and the flat causal claim; the quote only reports that about 60% of patients with acquired resistance to EGFR TKIs develop a new mutation in the drug target.

evidence.quote: Approximately 60% of patients with acquired resistance to the EGFR TKIs (erlotinib, gefitinib, and afatinib) develop a new mutation within the drug target.

module: 22.1 Principles of Chemotherapy: Mechanism of Action
original: The term "chemotherapy" was coined by German chemist Paul Ehrlich, who investigated the use of drugs to treat infectious diseases and was the first scientist to study animal models to screen chemicals for potential activity against diseases.
proposed: Paul Ehrlich is described as the founder of chemotherapy and received the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine.
why: Dropped coining the term, German chemist, infectious disease work and first animal screening models; the quote only calls Ehrlich the founder of chemotherapy and notes his Nobel Prize.

evidence.quote: One hundred years ago, Paul Ehrlich, the founder of chemotherapy, received the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine.

original: Cisplatin, for example, is FDA approved for the treatment of advanced ovarian cancer, testicular cancer, and bladder carcinoma, and is frequently used off-label for numerous other malignancies.
proposed: Cisplatin, for example, has an FDA label listing use in combination therapy for metastatic testicular tumors and as a single agent for advanced transitional cell bladder cancer no longer amenable to surgery or radiotherapy.
why: Dropped ovarian cancer and off-label use, which neither quote covers. The label quotes support the testicular and bladder indications.

evidence.quote: Metastatic Testicular Tumors In established combination therapy with other approved chemotherapeutic agents in patients with metastatic testicular tumors who have already received appropriate surgical and/or radio therapeutic procedures.

Advanced Bladder Cancer Cisplatin Injection is indicated as a single agent for patients with transitional cell bladder cancer which is no longer amenable to local treatments, such as surgery and/or radiotherapy.

original: The development of pyrimidine and purine analogs as potential antineoplastic agents evolved from the early presumption that nucleic acids are involved in growth control.
proposed: Numerous pyrimidine and purine analogs were synthesized in the late forties in G.H. Hitchings' group as potential nucleic acid antagonists.
why: Dropped the antineoplastic purpose and growth-control presumption; the quote gives only nucleic acid antagonism as the rationale and names Hitchings' group.

evidence.quote: Numerous pyrimidine and purine analogs were synthesized in the late forties in G.H. Hitchings' group as potential nucleic acid antagonists.

original: Drugs like bortezomib, docetaxel, etoposide, imatinib, sunitinib, sorafenib, and vinca alkaloids are metabolized by CYP3A4/5.
proposed: Docetaxel is metabolized by CYP3A4 in vitro, and CYP3A4 is the major enzyme responsible for the metabolism of imatinib.
why: Narrowed from the long drug list to the two drugs quoted. Docetaxel is shown in vitro; CYP3A5 and the other drugs are not covered.

evidence.quote: Metabolism Docetaxel is metabolized by the CYP3A4 isoenzyme in vitro [see Drug Interactions (7) ].
Elimination Metabolism CYP3A4 is the major enzyme responsible for metabolism of imatinib.

original: Cancer stem cells, stromal cells, and immune cells can be reprogrammed by malignant cells to secrete factors that support tumor progression and suppress apoptotic pathways.
proposed: Therapy-induced tumour secretome (TCS) can impact cancer stem cell expansion and tumour-associated immune cells to enable tumour regrowth, and in ovarian cancer adipose-derived stem cells interact with cancer cells and secrete soluble factors that can promote metastasis and chemoresistance.
why: Replaced reprogramming and apoptosis suppression, which no quote states, with what the quotes show: secreted factors affecting stem and immune cells, and stem cell secretions promoting metastasis and chemoresistance in ovarian cancer.

evidence.quote: We also highlight recent evidence describing how therapy-induced TCS can impact cancer stem cell (CSC) expansion and tumour-associated immune cells to enable tumour regrowth and antitumour immunity.

Adipose-derived stem cell in the tumor microenvironment of ovarian cancer, as a key player, interacts with ovarian cancer cells to form the cancer-associated fibroblasts and cancer-associated adipocytes, and secretes soluble factors to activate tumor cell signaling, which can promote ovarian cancer metastasis and chemoresistance.

original: Elevated expressions of repair system genes are often associated with chemotherapy resistance and represent potential molecular targets for overcoming resistance.
proposed: Upregulation of the DNA damage response (repair) machinery has been linked to chemoresistance across cancers, and increased DNA damage repair capacity is a key mechanism underlying oxaliplatin resistance.
why: Dropped 'often' and the claim about molecular targets for overcoming resistance, which no quote states. Kept the link to chemoresistance and the oxaliplatin example.

evidence.quote: Previous reports have linked upregulation of the DNA damage response (DDR) machinery to chemoresistance and immune evasion across cancers.
An increased capacity for DNA damage repair is a key mechanism underlying oxaliplatin resistance.

original: Involving other transport proteins such as multidrug resistance-associated proteins (MRPs) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), which have different substrate specificities.
proposed: Involving other transport proteins such as breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), which confers resistance to multiple drugs, including mitoxantrone, methotrexate, daunorubicin and doxorubicin, through the control of their efflux.
why: Dropped MRPs and the comparison of substrate specificities; the quote lists only the drugs whose efflux the BCRP record says it controls.

evidence.quote: It confers to cells a resistance to multiple drugs and other xenobiotics including mitoxantrone, pheophorbide, camptothecin, methotrexate, azidothymidine, and the anthracyclines daunorubicin and doxorubicin, through the control of their efflux (PubMed:11306452, PubMed:12477054, PubMed:15670731, PubMed:18056989, PubMed:31254042).

original: Mediated primarily by P-glycoprotein overexpression, which pumps various structurally unrelated drugs out of the cell, including anthracyclines, vinca alkaloids, and taxanes.
proposed: Mediated by P-glycoprotein, an energy-dependent efflux pump responsible for decreased drug accumulation in multidrug-resistant cells.
why: Dropped 'primarily', overexpression and the named drug classes (anthracyclines, vinca alkaloids, taxanes), which the quote does not state; kept the efflux pump role in multidrug-resistant cells.

evidence.quote: Energy-dependent efflux pump responsible for decreased drug accumulation in multidrug-resistant cells (PubMed:2897240, PubMed:35970996, PubMed:9038218).

original: Early intervention by perioperative multidisciplinary teams has been shown to decrease adverse events during neoadjuvant chemotherapy, particularly for esophageal and other complex cancers requiring intensive perioperative management.
proposed: In one study, adverse events during chemotherapy, especially oral complications, were significantly decreased when the PERiO intervention started before neoadjuvant chemotherapy, and in another the OPERA intervention significantly reduced chemotherapy-related adverse events.
why: Replaced 'multidisciplinary teams' and esophageal/complex cancers, which the quotes do not name, with the two named perioperative interventions and their reported reductions in adverse events.

evidence.quote: The adverse event rate during chemotherapy, especially oral complications, was significantly decreased in the PERiO Intervention started before the NAC group (P = 0.007).
The OPERA intervention significantly reduced the incidence of chemotherapy-related adverse events (P=0.002).

original: The FOxTROT trial results have prompted implementation of novel treatment pathways, demonstrating that neoadjuvant chemotherapy with oxaliplatin and 5-fluorouracil can be successfully integrated into standard care with appropriate multidisciplinary team modifications.
proposed: The FOxTROT trial results have prompted implementation of a novel treatment pathway: the trial met its primary endpoint, with fewer patients having recurrent or residual disease at 2 years with neoadjuvant chemotherapy than with control (16.8% vs. 21.2%), and 64 patients have been commenced on the new pathway.
why: Dropped successful integration into standard care, oxaliplatin/5-FU and team modifications, which no quote states. Kept the endpoint result and the 64 patients started on the pathway.

evidence.quote: The trial met its primary endpoint with fewer patients experiencing recurrent or residual disease at 2 years with NAC compared with the control (16.8% vs. 21.2%, risk ratio = 0.74, p = 0.042).
To date 64 patients have been commenced on the novel pathway following presentation and adoption of the FOxTROT trial results.

original: Raloxifene: Raloxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that has estrogen-like effects (agonism) on bone and the cardiovascular system but antiestrogen activity (antagonism) on breast and uterus tissue.
proposed: Raloxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM), an estrogen agonist/antagonist, and preclinical data show that it is an estrogen antagonist in uterine and breast tissues.
why: Dropped estrogen-like effects on bone and the cardiovascular system, which the quotes do not state. Kept the SERM class and the preclinical antagonism in uterine and breast tissues.

evidence.quote: Raloxifene is an estrogen agonist/antagonist, commonly referred to as a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM).
Preclinical data demonstrate that raloxifene is an estrogen antagonist in uterine and breast tissues.

original: Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) medication used to treat breast cancer in both men and women and as a prophylactic agent against breast cancer in women.
proposed: Tamoxifen citrate tablets are effective in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer in women and men and are indicated to reduce the incidence of breast cancer in women at high risk.
why: Dropped the SERM label and the broader 'treat breast cancer' and 'prophylactic' wording; the label quotes cover metastatic disease in both sexes and risk reduction in high-risk women.

evidence.quote: Tamoxifen citrate tablets are effective in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer in women and men.
Tamoxifen citrate tablets are indicated to reduce the incidence of breast cancer in women at high risk for breast cancer.

original: Anastrozole, a selective aromatase inhibitor, is available as a 1 mg tablet, which is to be taken orally once a day, with or without food.
proposed: Anastrozole is dosed as one 1 mg tablet taken once a day, with or without food.
why: Dropped 'selective aromatase inhibitor' and the oral route, which the quotes do not state; the dose, daily schedule and food statement are quoted.

evidence.quote: The dose of anastrozole tablet is one 1 mg tablet taken once a day.
Anastrozole tablets can be taken with or without food.

original: Aromatase (estrogen synthetase) is a member of the cytochrome P450 superfamily of monooxygenases and catalyzes the demethylation of androgens' carbon 19, producing phenolic 18-carbon estrogens.
proposed: Aromatase is a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase that catalyzes the conversion of C19 androgens (androstenedione and testosterone) to the C18 estrogens estrone and estradiol, through successive oxidations at C19.
why: Dropped superfamily membership, the 'estrogen synthetase' name and 'demethylation', which the quotes do not use; kept the P450 monooxygenase, C19-to-C18 conversion and successive C19 oxidations.

evidence.quote: A cytochrome P450 monooxygenase that catalyzes the conversion of C19 androgens, androst-4-ene-3,17-dione (androstenedione) and testosterone to the C18 estrogens, estrone and estradiol, respectively (PubMed:27702664, PubMed:2848247).
Catalyzes three successive oxidations of C19 androgens: two conventional oxidations at C19 yielding 19-hydroxy and 19-oxo/19-aldehyde derivatives,

original: Letrozole is also a selective aromatase inhibitor.
proposed: Letrozole is also a nonsteroidal competitive aromatase inhibitor that selectively inhibits gonadal steroidogenesis, with no significant effect on adrenal mineralocorticoid or glucocorticoid synthesis.
why: The quotes do not call letrozole a 'selective aromatase inhibitor'. They give competitive aromatase inhibition and selectivity for gonadal steroidogenesis, so the sentence states those instead.

evidence.quote: Letrozole is a nonsteroidal competitive inhibitor of the aromatase enzyme system; it inhibits the conversion of androgens to estrogens.
Letrozole selectively inhibits gonadal steroidogenesis but has no significant effect on adrenal mineralocorticoid or glucocorticoid synthesis.

original: Enzalutamide is a third generation, oral nonsteroidal antiandrogen used in the treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
proposed: Enzalutamide (XTANDI) is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer.
why: Dropped 'third generation', oral, nonsteroidal and metastatic, which the label quote does not state; kept androgen receptor inhibitor and the castration-resistant prostate cancer indication.

evidence.quote: XTANDI is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with: • castration-resistant prostate cancer.

original: Therapy with enzalutamide has been shown to prolong relapse free as well as overall survival in men with metastatic, castration-resistant prostate cancer who had previously failed other forms of treatment.
proposed: Therapy with enzalutamide has been shown to prolong overall survival: a statistically significant improvement in overall survival was demonstrated at the pre-specified interim analysis in patients on the enzalutamide arm compared with the placebo arm.
why: Dropped relapse-free survival and the prior-treatment population, which the quote does not state; the quote gives a significant overall survival improvement versus placebo at the interim analysis.

evidence.quote: A statistically significant improvement in overall survival was demonstrated at the pre-specified interim analysis at the time of 520 deaths in patients on the XTANDI arm compared to patients on the placebo arm ( Table 9 and Figure 1 ).

original: The commercial names and year of approval in the United States of the currently available forms of GnRH agonists and antagonists are: leuprolide, also called leuprorelin (Lupron: 1985), goserelin (Zoladex: 1989), histrelin (Supprelin, Vantas: 1991 and 2004), triptorelin (Trelstar: 2000).
proposed: Among the currently available forms of GnRH agonists and antagonists, triptorelin (Trelstar) was originally approved in the United States on 15 June 2000.
why: Dropped leuprolide, goserelin and histrelin and their years; the only quote shows an original approval date of 15 June 2000, which the record ties to Trelstar.

evidence.quote: ORIG 1 AP 20000615

original: The principal mechanism of action of LHRH antagonists is the competitive occupancy of LHRH receptors, but recent experimental evidence documents that treatment with the LHRH antagonist cetrorelix also downregulates pituitary LHRH receptors in rats and decreases the levels of mRNA for LHRH receptors.
proposed: Experimental evidence shows that prolonged treatment with the LHRH antagonist cetrorelix causes a marked decrease in the levels of LHRH receptors and in expression of the LHRH receptor gene, including a 75-80% decrease in LHRH receptor mRNA compared with controls.
why: Dropped the principal competitive-occupancy mechanism, 'recent', rats and pituitary, which the quotes do not name. Kept cetrorelix lowering LHRH receptor levels, gene expression and mRNA.

evidence.quote: In conclusion, these data demonstrate that prolonged administration of LHRH antagonists such as Cetrorelix causes an impairment of gonadotropin secretion and a marked decrease in the levels of LHRH receptors as well as in the expression of the LHRH receptor gene.
Treatment with Cetrorelix pamoate depot led to a 75-80% decrease in the levels of 5.0- and 4.5-kilobase forms of LHRH receptor mRNA compared to those in the control group.

original: Abiraterone is associated with an appreciable rate of serum enzyme elevation during therapy and with rare but potentially severe instances of acute liver injury with jaundice.
proposed: The abiraterone acetate label warns that hepatotoxicity can be severe and fatal and that liver function should be monitored, with dosing modified, interrupted or discontinued as recommended.
why: Dropped serum enzyme elevation, jaundice and 'rare'; the label quote states severe, fatal hepatotoxicity and the need for liver monitoring and dose changes.

evidence.quote: Hepatotoxicity: Can be severe and fatal. Monitor liver function and modify, interrupt, or discontinue abiraterone acetate dosing as recommended. ( 5.3 )

original: The use of ADT in prostate cancer patients corresponded with a significant increase in cardiovascular morbidity associated with AMI and with nonfatal events.
proposed: Several observational studies suggest that the use of ADT in prostate cancer patients is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events, although most published studies report that ADT is not linked to greater cardiovascular mortality.
why: Softened 'significant increase' and dropped the AMI and nonfatal detail. The quote says observational studies suggest more cardiovascular events, with most reporting no greater cardiovascular mortality.

evidence.quote: Several observational studies suggest an increased risk of diabetes and cardiovascular events, although most published studies report that ADT is not linked to greater cardiovascular mortality.

original: ENZ is moderately effective in CRPC patients who were pretreated with chemotherapy and abiraterone acetate.
proposed: In one trial comparing cabazitaxel with an androgen-signaling-targeted inhibitor, the inhibitor arm had a median progression-free survival of 2.7 months and a PSA response in 13.5% of patients, compared with 4.4 months and 35.7% with cabazitaxel.
why: The quote names an androgen-signaling-targeted inhibitor arm, not ENZ, and gives no 'moderately effective' judgment or prior-therapy detail. The sentence reports the numbers and the comparison.

evidence.quote: The median progression-free survival was 4.4 months with cabazitaxel and 2.7 months with an androgen-signaling-targeted inhibitor (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.40 to 0.68; P<0.001), a prostate-specific antigen response occurred in 35.7% and 13.5% of the patients, respectively (P<0.001), and tumor response was noted in 36.5% and 11.5% (P = 0.004).

original: Inevitable Resistance: Most patients eventually develop resistance to targeted therapies.
proposed: Acquired resistance to cancer treatments limits their efficacy and accounts for therapeutic failure in most patients.
why: Dropped 'inevitable' and 'targeted therapies'; the quote speaks of acquired therapeutic resistance to cancer treatments in general, accounting for failure in most patients.

evidence.quote: Development of acquired therapeutic resistance limits the efficacy of cancer treatments and accounts for therapeutic failure in most patients.

original: In cancer cells, cross-linking CD20 can induce cell cycle arrest, inhibit DNA synthesis, activate caspases, and induce apoptosis.
proposed: In cancer cells, cross-linking CD20 at the cell surface can activate numerous intracellular responses and increase susceptibility to anticancer drugs such as docetaxel and gemcitabine.
why: Dropped cell cycle arrest, DNA synthesis inhibition, caspases and apoptosis, which the quotes do not name; the quote states numerous intracellular responses and increased drug susceptibility.

evidence.quote: The extracellular actuation by surface CD20 crosslinking boosts robust activations of numerous intracellular responses, and promotes cancer cell susceptibility to various anticancer drugs, including docetaxel (microtubule stabilizer), gemcitabine (nucleoside analogue) and GDC-0980 (PI3K/mTOR inhibitor).

original: Rb pathway alterations: Loss of Rb function or alterations in upstream regulators can confer resistance.
proposed: Rb pathway alterations: RB1 loss has been linked to therapy resistance in breast cancer models, and MYC amplification confers resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors in bladder, prostate and breast cancer cells by causing RB1 deficiency.
why: Narrowed from a general claim about Rb function and upstream regulators to the two named cases: RB1 loss in breast cancer models and MYC-driven RB1 deficiency in CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance.

evidence.quote: Here, we demonstrate that MYC amplification confers resistance to CDK4/6i in bladder, prostate and breast cancer cells. Mechanistically, MYC binds to the promoter of the E3 ubiquitin ligase KLHL42 and enhances its transcription, leading to RB1 deficiency by inducing both phosphorylated and total pRB1 ubiquitination and degradation.

Whole-genome sequencing of breast cancer models and paired primary-metastatic samples demonstrated that active APOBEC3 mutagenesis promoted therapy resistance through characteristic alterations such as RB1 loss.

original: Ribociclib: A unique cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor that is used in combination with aromatase inhibitors in the treatment of postmenopausal women with metastatic breast cancer.
proposed: Ribociclib is a CDK4/6 inhibitor indicated, in combination with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy, for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
why: Dropped 'unique' and 'postmenopausal women'; the label says adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer, and the second quote names ribociclib as a CDK4/6 inhibitor.

evidence.quote: KISQALI is indicated for the treatment of adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with: an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy; or fulvestrant as initial endocrine-based therapy or following disease progression on endocrine therapy.
12.1 Mechanism of Action Ribociclib is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4 and 6.

original: The cyclin kinases 4 and 6 regulate the cellular transition from the G1 to the S phase of the cell cycle acting through the retinoblastoma protein (Rb) pathway.
proposed: Cyclin-dependent kinase 6 promotes the transition from G1 to S phase of the cell cycle and phosphorylates the retinoblastoma protein (Rb/RB1).
why: Narrowed from CDK4 and CDK6 to CDK6, the only kinase the quote covers; kept the G1/S transition and Rb phosphorylation it states.

evidence.quote: Serine/threonine-protein kinase involved in the control of the cell cycle and differentiation; promotes G1/S transition. Phosphorylates pRB/RB1 and NPM1.

original: During the prevascular phase, when angiogenic activity is absent or insufficient, tumors remain small, with volumes measured in a few cubic millimeters.
proposed: Small, circumscribed, relatively avascular tumors were found in the brains of rabbits that were copper-depleted by diet and penicillamine treatment.
why: Dropped the general prevascular-phase claim and the volume in cubic millimeters; the quote reports small, relatively avascular tumors in copper-depleted rabbit brains.

evidence.quote: By contrast, small, circumscribed, relatively avascular tumors were found in the brains of rabbits copper-depleted by diet and penicillamine treatment (CDPT).

original: Hypertension: The overall incidence of significantly raised blood pressure was 8% among patients receiving bevacizumab, with a significantly increased risk compared to controls.
proposed: Hypertension is a reported adverse effect of bevacizumab: the incidence of grade 3-4 hypertension differs among the malignancies in which it is given, and in one study hypertension was reported in 32 (50.8%) patients receiving bevacizumab.
why: Dropped the 8% figure and the significantly increased risk versus controls, which neither quote states; kept the variable incidence by malignancy and one study's 50.8%.

evidence.quote: The incidence of grade 3-4 hypertension differs among the various malignancies in which bevacizumab is administered, possibly because of drug interactions with co-administered chemotherapy drugs.
Hypertension was reported in 32 (50.8%) patients receiving bevacizumab.

original: Thromboembolism: The use of bevacizumab was significantly associated with an increased risk of developing venous thromboembolism in cancer patients.
proposed: In trials comparing bevacizumab plus chemotherapy with chemotherapy alone, venous thromboembolisms were more common with bevacizumab (5% vs 3% in one trial), and thromboembolic events of grade 3 or higher were more frequent in another (8% vs 1%).
why: Dropped 'significantly' and the general cancer-patient claim; the quotes give event rates from two trials without a significance test for the venous thromboembolism result.

evidence.quote: Grade 3-5 bleeding or haemorrhage (eight [2%] vs one [<1%]), gastrointestinal perforation (seven [2%] vs three [<1%]), and venous thromboembolisms (19 [5%] vs 12 [3%]) were more common in the bevacizumab plus chemotherapy group than in the chemotherapy alone group.

Bevacizumab, as compared with chemotherapy alone, was associated with an increased incidence of hypertension of grade 2 or higher (25% vs. 2%), thromboembolic events of grade 3 or higher (8% vs. 1%), and gastrointestinal fistulas of grade 3 or higher (3% vs. 0%).

original: Tumor angiogenesis is required for tumors to grow beyond a few millimeters in size and for metastatic spread.
proposed: Metastasis appears to depend on angiogenesis, along with tumor cell motility, dedifferentiation, and local invasion.
why: Dropped the 'beyond a few millimeters' growth claim and 'required'; the quote only says metastasis appears to depend on angiogenesis among other factors.

evidence.quote: Metastasis appears to depend upon tumor cell motility, dedifferentiation, local invasion, and angiogenesis.

original: A classic example is the T790M mutation in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which occurs in over half of patients treated with first-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) like erlotinib or gefitinib.
proposed: A classic example is the T790M mutation in EGFR, a secondary exon 20 mutation that accounts for approximately 60% of cases of acquired resistance to EGFR TKIs such as erlotinib and gefitinib.
why: Dropped NSCLC and 'over half of patients treated'; the quotes give about 60% of acquired-resistance cases, not of all treated patients.

evidence.quote: Approximately 60% of patients with acquired resistance to the EGFR TKIs (erlotinib, gefitinib, and afatinib) develop a new mutation within the drug target. This mutation-T790M-has been shown to alter drug binding and enzymatic activity of the mutant EGF receptor.
In this context, a secondary EGFR mutation in exon 20, namely T790M, has been found to be responsible for approximately 60% of cases of acquired resistance.

original: Cancer cell spheroids allow study of the tumor microenvironment and how it affects the ability of drugs to penetrate and kill tumor cells.
proposed: Cancer cell spheroids are a three-dimensional in vitro model that incorporates microenvironmental influences to study mechanisms of drug resistance in breast cancer, and in one study disrupting hyaluronan production facilitated drug penetration into tumor spheroids.
why: Tied spheroids as a study model to the review quote (breast cancer drug resistance) and one study of drug penetration; neither quote mentions drug killing of tumor cells.

evidence.quote: By disrupting hyaluronan production, this compound facilitated drug penetration into tumor spheroids and reduced the expression of drug efflux pumps, thereby increasing intracellular drug accumulation.

This review discusses three-dimensional (3D) in vitro model systems which incorporate microenvironmental influences to study mechanisms of drug resistance in breast cancer. These bioengineered models include spheroid-based models, biomaterial-based models such as polymeric scaffolds and hydrogels, and microfluidic chip-based models.

original: Cancer cells employ diverse strategies to evade therapeutic interventions, which can be broadly categorized into intrinsic (primary) resistance that exists prior to treatment initiation, and acquired resistance that develops through selective pressure during therapy.
proposed: For anti-angiogenic agents targeting the VEGF pathway, two general models of tumor resistance have been proposed: intrinsic (preexisting) non-responsiveness, and adaptive (evasive) resistance, which occurs after a prolonged application of a drug.
why: The quote covers anti-angiogenic agents targeting VEGF, not all therapies, and does not mention selective pressure; the sentence states the two proposed models as described.

evidence.quote: Two general models of tumor resistance to anti-angiogenic agents targeting the VEGF pathway have been proposed: an adaptive (evasive) resistance, which occurs after a prolonged application of a drug (providing a period of tumor control), or intrinsic one (preexisting) non-responsiveness despite the presence of an active agent, showing no therapeutic benefit.

original: Common examples include activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway in response to MAPK pathway inhibition, or engagement of alternative receptor tyrosine kinases.
proposed: Examples include engagement of alternative receptor tyrosine kinases and activation of PI3K/Akt signaling in response to EGFR inhibition, and EGFR and AXL cooperatively rescuing signaling from RET inhibition in PR2 cells.
why: Replaced PI3K/AKT activation in response to MAPK inhibition with the quoted contexts: EGFR inhibition and RET inhibition. Neither quote concerns MAPK inhibition.

evidence.quote: While in an EGFR-independent manner, dysregulation of other receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) or abnormal activation of downstream compounds both have compensatory functions against the inhibition of EGFR through triggering phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling axes.
Thus, EGFR and AXL cooperatively rescued signaling from RET inhibition in the PR2 cells.

original: Drug Metabolism: Alterations in drug-metabolizing enzymes can lead to drug inactivation or failure to convert prodrugs into active metabolites.
proposed: Drug Metabolism: Drug-metabolizing enzymes present in tumorous tissues can cause resistance by metabolizing drugs and rendering them inactive, and genetic variants that change the activity of these enzymes, in prodrug activation or drug inactivation, may determine the lack of response to anticancer chemotherapy.
why: Framed as anticancer drugs and chemotherapy, as the quotes are, rather than targeted therapies. 'Alterations' became genetic variants, and prodrug failure is reduced to a possible lack of response.

evidence.quote: When present in tumorous tissues, they cause resistance by metabolizing the drugs and rendering them inactive.

Regarding pro-drug activation or drug inactivation, genetic variants are responsible for changes in the activity of drug-metabolizing enzymes, which affect drug clearance and may determine the lack of response to anticancer chemotherapy.

original: Immune Evasion: Tumors can recruit immunosuppressive cells including myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), regulatory T cells (Tregs), and M2-polarized macrophages that create an immunosuppressive TME.
proposed: Immune Evasion: The immunosuppressive milieu within tumors consists of regulatory T cells (Tregs), M2 macrophages, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), and in one mouse model (MC38 tumors in ovariectomized mice) these populations increased.
why: Dropped recruitment by tumors, which neither quote states. Kept the three cell types named as forming the immunosuppressive milieu and the mouse finding that they increased.

evidence.quote: This restriction of efficacy may be due to an intratumoral immunosuppressive milieu, consisting of regulatory T cells, M2 macrophages, and myeloid derived suppressor cells.

The PD-L1+ M2-like macrophage, regulatory T (Treg) cell, and myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) populations significantly increased, and the population of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells declined in MC38 tumors in ovariectomized mice, which were all reversed in ovariectomized mice with E2 supplementation.

original: In EGFR-mutant NSCLC, MET amplification can activate parallel signaling pathways that maintain cell survival despite EGFR inhibition.
proposed: MET amplification has been reported as an EGFR-independent mechanism of resistance that involves activation of alternative signaling pathways, and is listed among the less common mechanisms of acquired resistance.
why: Dropped EGFR-mutant NSCLC and the survival-maintenance wording, which the quotes do not state; kept MET amplification as an EGFR-independent mechanism activating alternative pathways.

evidence.quote: EGFR-independent resistance includes the activation of alternative signaling pathways, such as MET amplification and HER2 mutations, and histological transformation.
Less common mechanisms of acquired resistance include MET amplification, ERBB2 amplification, transformation to small-cell lung cancer, and others.

original: Resistance occurs through enhanced activity of nucleotide excision repair (NER) and homologous recombination repair (HRR) mechanisms.
proposed: Resistance can occur through restored homologous recombination repair: loss of DYNLL1 restores homologous recombination in BRCA1-mutant cells, inducing resistance to platinum drugs and PARP inhibitors, and SENP5 has been implicated in HR-mediated DNA damage repair and cancer resistance.
why: Dropped nucleotide excision repair, which neither quote addresses, and the claim of enhanced activity in general; the quotes support homologous recombination in two examples.

evidence.quote: The loss of DYNLL1 enables DNA end resection and restores homologous recombination in BRCA1-mutant cells, thereby inducing resistance to platinum drugs and inhibitors of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase.

CONCLUSION: Our findings revealed novel role of SENP5 in HR mediated DNA damage repair and cancer resistance, which could be applied as potent prognostic marker and intervention target for cancer radiotherapy.

original: Similarly, in chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML), BCR-ABL kinase activity is frequently restored through mutations in the ABL kinase domain in patients who relapse on imatinib treatment.
proposed: Similarly, in chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), patients who relapse on imatinib can do so because of acquired ABL1 kinase domain mutations; in one study of 83 patients tested, 44 (53%) were positive for one or more tyrosine kinase domain mutations.
why: Dropped restored BCR-ABL kinase activity and 'frequently'; the quotes give imatinib relapse due to acquired ABL1 kinase domain mutations and one study's 53% mutation rate.

evidence.quote: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients who relapse on imatinib due to acquired ABL1 kinase domain mutations are successfully treated with second-generation ABL1-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (ABL-TKIs) such as dasatinib, nilotinib or ponatinib.
TKD mutation study was done on 83 patients. Of these 44 (53%) were positive for one or more mutations.

original: Target Mutations: Cancer cells frequently develop second-site or gatekeeper mutations in the drug target itself.
proposed: Target Mutations: Cancer cells can develop gatekeeper mutations, such as EGFR T790M and FGFR gatekeeper mutations, that drive resistance; EGFR T790M can arise by selection of pre-existing clones or by genetic evolution of initially T790M-negative drug-tolerant cells.
why: Dropped 'frequently' and 'second-site', which no quote supports. The quotes show EGFR T790M and FGFR gatekeeper mutations driving resistance, and two routes by which T790M arises.

evidence.quote: Here we observe that acquired resistance caused by the EGFR(T790M) gatekeeper mutation can occur either by selection of pre-existing EGFR(T790M)-positive clones or via genetic evolution of initially EGFR(T790M)-negative drug-tolerant cells.
The chemical compound LY2874455 has the potential to overcome drug resistance driven by FGFR gatekeeper mutations.

original: Upstream Activation: Amplification or mutation of upstream activators can restore signaling despite target inhibition.
proposed: Upstream Activation: Alterations upstream of the target, such as secondary NRAS mutations in resistance to BRAF inhibitors, can lead to reactivation of the MAPK pathway, and upstream RTK and SHP2-mediated bypass signaling has been reported to limit response durability.
why: Dropped amplification, which the quotes do not mention; the BRAF quote supports upstream alterations reactivating MAPK signaling and the second quote supports upstream RTK and SHP2 bypass signaling limiting durability.

evidence.quote: So far, a number of resistance mechanisms have been identified, including secondary NRAS mutations and BRAF alternative splicing, leading to reactivation of the MAPK pathway. Other alterations, both upstream and downstream of BRAF can have the same effect, and activation of alternative pathways can also play a role in resistance to BRAF inhibitors.

Yet response durability is limited by on-target switch-II pocket mutations, upstream RTK and SHP2-mediated bypass signaling, downstream MAPK and PI3K-AKT reactivation, phenotypic plasticity, and adverse modulation by co-occurring STK11, KEAP1, and TP53 alterations.

original: Immuno-PET: Radiolabeled antibodies such as 89Zr-atezolizumab enable assessment of PD-L1 expression throughout the body.
proposed: Immuno-PET with 89Zr-atezolizumab has been used to image patients before atezolizumab therapy: in 22 patients across three tumor types, the PET signal, a function of tracer exposure and target expression, was high in lymphoid tissues and at sites of inflammation, and in tumorgrafts uptake was significantly higher in index than control tumors.
why: Dropped 'enable assessment of PD-L1 expression throughout the body', which the quotes do not state. They report a PET signal that reflects target expression, found in specific tissues in 22 patients, and a tumorgraft uptake difference.

evidence.quote: We imaged 22 patients across three tumor types before the start of atezolizumab therapy. The PET signal, a function of tracer exposure and target expression, was high in lymphoid tissues and at sites of inflammation.
iPET revealed significantly higher 89Zr-atezolizumab uptake in index than control tumorgrafts.

original: PET Imaging: Positron emission tomography using specific tracers can assess therapeutic target expression across all disease sites.
proposed: PET Imaging: Noninvasive molecular imaging techniques such as PET and SPECT provide information on the whole-body distribution of radiolabeled antibodies and can potentially elucidate drug target expression, and radionuclide imaging has been proposed for repeatable whole-body assessment of EGFR-family expression.
why: Dropped 'across all disease sites' and the flat claim of assessing expression. The quotes say PET and SPECT give whole-body distribution and can potentially elucidate target expression, with EGFR-family imaging as one example.

evidence.quote: Radionuclide molecular imaging can be a key asset for the detection of overexpression of EGFR-family members. It meets the need for repeatable whole-body assessment of the molecular disease profile, solving problems of heterogeneity and expression alterations over time.

Noninvasive molecular imaging techniques, such as SPECT and PET, provide information on the whole-body distribution of radiolabeled mAbs and antibody-related therapeutics. Molecular antibody imaging can potentially elucidate drug target expression, tracer uptake in the tumor, tumor saturation, and heterogeneity for these parameters within the tumor.

original: The National Cancer Institute has established a 30-point checklist to determine whether omics-based tests are ready for use in prospective clinical trials involving patient-care decisions.
proposed: The National Cancer Institute has developed a checklist of criteria that can be used to determine the readiness of omics-based tests for guiding patient care in clinical trials.
why: Dropped '30-point' and 'prospective'; the quotes say the NCI developed a checklist of criteria for test readiness in clinical trials, without a count.

evidence.quote: The US National Cancer Institute (NCI), in collaboration with scientists representing multiple areas of expertise relevant to 'omics'-based test development, has developed a checklist of criteria that can be used to determine the readiness of omics-based tests for guiding patient care in clinical trials.
The US National Cancer Institute plans to refer to these guidelines for review of proposals for studies involving omics tests, and it is hoped that other sponsors will adopt the checklist as well.

original: Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB): High TMB has been associated with increased neoantigen load and enhanced immune recognition, predicting better response to immune checkpoint inhibitors across different cancer types.
proposed: Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB): In an analysis of more than 1,000 checkpoint inhibitor-treated patients across seven tumor types, clonal TMB was the strongest predictor of response, followed by total TMB and CXCL9 expression, and in another study pathological responses correlated significantly with tumor mutational burden.
why: Dropped neoantigen load, enhanced immune recognition and 'across different cancer types' as a general claim; the quotes give one seven-tumor-type analysis and a correlation with pathological response.

evidence.quote: Here, we collated whole-exome and transcriptomic data for >1,000 CPI-treated patients across seven tumor types, utilizing standardized bioinformatics workflows and clinical outcome criteria to validate multivariable predictors of CPI sensitization. Clonal tumor mutation burden (TMB) was the strongest predictor of CPI response, followed by total TMB and CXCL9 expression.
Pathological responses correlate significantly with microsatellite instability status, PD-L1 expression, and tumor mutational burden.

original: Antigen Spreading: Therapies inducing immunogenic cell death promote epitope spreading, expanding the immune response beyond initially targeted antigens.
proposed: Antigen Spreading: In some studies, treatments that induced immunogenic cell death led to antigen spreading; for example, antigen-activated dCAR T cells induced immunogenic cell death, which stimulated endogenous CD8+ T cells and enhanced their antigen-spreading capacity.
why: Dropped epitope spreading beyond the initially targeted antigens and the general claim; the quotes describe antigen spreading after immunogenic cell death in specific combined and dCAR T treatments.

evidence.quote: The combined treatment achieved a synergistic effect, which not only reduced immunosuppressive Tregs but also induced immunogenic cell death, leading to antigen spreading and reducing immune evasion caused by tumor antigenic modulation.

Crucially, antigen-activated dCAR T cells sustained high levels of interferon-γ production, which induced immunogenic cell death in tumor cells and activated conventional dendritic cells. This, in turn, stimulated endogenous CD8+ T cells, enhancing their antigen-spreading capacity and aiding in the clearance of abscopal antigen-negative tumors.

original: Emerging Checkpoints: Clinical trials are evaluating inhibitors of LAG-3, TIM-3, TIGIT, VISTA, and other co-inhibitory molecules.
proposed: Emerging Checkpoints: Clinical trials of LAG-3 inhibitors include a phase II trial of relatlimab (anti-LAG-3) and nivolumab with chemotherapy in gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, and a phase IIR trial with an anti-LAG3 arm.
why: Dropped TIM-3, TIGIT, VISTA and other co-inhibitory molecules; the quotes name only LAG-3 trials. Present tense avoids implying all are ongoing.

evidence.quote: This is a multicentre, phase IIR, double non-comparative arm trial, with an initial safety run for the anti-LAG3 arm.

A Randomized, Open-label, Phase II Clinical Trial of Relatlimab (Anti-LAG-3) and Nivolumab in Combination With Chemotherapy Versus Nivolumab in Combination With Chemotherapy as First-Line Treatment in Patients With Gastric or Gastroesophageal Junction Adenocarcinoma

original: PROTACs tag specific cancer-causing proteins for degradation by the cell's normal machinery, offering a way to target previously "undruggable" proteins.
proposed: PROTACs are bifunctional molecules that recruit a target protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together to trigger degradation of the target by the ubiquitin-proteasome system, and targeted protein degradation has been described as unlocking therapeutic possibilities for previously "undruggable" targets such as MYC, STAT3 and mutant KRAS G12C.
why: Replaced 'tag cancer-causing proteins' with the quoted recruitment mechanism, and attributed the undruggable-target claim to targeted protein degradation, since that quote does not name PROTACs.

evidence.quote: A bifunctional PROTAC molecule with two covalently-linked ligands recruits target protein and E3 ubiquitin ligase together to trigger proteasomal degradation of target protein by the ubiquitin-proteasome system.

This approach has unlocked therapeutic possibilities for previously "undruggable" targets, including transcription factors like MYC and STAT3, mutant oncoproteins such as KRAS G12C, and scaffolding molecules lacking conventional binding pockets.

original: Protein Degraders: PROTACs (proteolysis-targeting chimeras) and molecular glues induce selective degradation of target proteins, including previously "undruggable" targets.
proposed: Protein Degraders: PROTACs (proteolysis targeting chimeras) and molecular glues are described as offering highly selective control of target inhibition, and targeted protein degradation strategies have been used to tackle targets deemed undruggable with traditional small molecule inhibitors.
why: Softened 'induce selective degradation' and the link to undruggable targets; the first quote speaks of selective control of target inhibition, and the second names targeted protein degradation, not PROTACs.

evidence.quote: One of the major improvements that PROTAC (proteolysis targeting chimera) and molecular glue technology can exert is highly selective control of target inhibition.
Targeted protein degradation (TPD) strategies have revolutionized how scientists tackle challenging protein targets deemed undruggable with traditional small molecule inhibitors.

original: Stromal Targeting: Inhibiting cancer-associated fibroblasts and disrupting tumor-stroma interactions improves drug delivery and immune cell infiltration.
proposed: Stromal Targeting: Modulating cancer-associated fibroblasts and targeting extracellular matrix components are being examined for their potential to enhance drug penetration and improve therapeutic efficacy; in one study, enhanced accumulation of Exos-PH20@Cur in the tumor core came with increased CD8+ T cell infiltration.
why: Softened 'improves' to potential, and dropped CAF inhibition. The review quote supports drug penetration; the study quote supports CD8+ infiltration for one agent.

evidence.quote: Strategies for stromal remodeling, including modulation of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs) activation states, and targeting extracellular matrix (ECM) components, are examined for their potential to enhance drug penetration and improve therapeutic efficacy.
As a result, the enhanced accumulation of Exos-PH20@Cur in tumor core, along with increased CD8+ T cells infiltration, contributed to effective cytotoxic inhibition on cancer cells.

original: The combination of anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-1 antibodies has shown improved outcomes in melanoma and other cancers, though with increased toxicity that requires careful management.
proposed: In one trial, nivolumab plus ipilimumab had a longer median progression-free survival than ipilimumab alone (11.5 vs 2.9 months), but grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 55.0% of patients on the combination, compared with 16.3% on nivolumab and 27.3% on ipilimumab.
why: Dropped melanoma and other cancers and the anti-CTLA-4/anti-PD-1 class wording, which the quotes do not state; kept the progression-free survival result and the higher rate of serious adverse events.

evidence.quote: The median progression-free survival was 11.5 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 8.9 to 16.7) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab, as compared with 2.9 months (95% CI, 2.8 to 3.4) with ipilimumab (hazard ratio for death or disease progression, 0.42; 99.5% CI, 0.31 to 0.57; P<0.001)

Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or 4 occurred in 16.3% of the patients in the nivolumab group, 55.0% of those in the nivolumab-plus-ipilimumab group, and 27.3% of those in the ipilimumab group.

original: Vertical Targeting: Combining drugs that target different nodes within the same pathway (e.g., RAF plus MEK inhibitors in BRAF-mutant melanoma) achieves more complete pathway inhibition and delays resistance.
proposed: Vertical Targeting: Combining BRAF and MEK inhibitors may give a synergistic effect in RAF-regulated and RAF-dependent variants, and combination strategies with dabrafenib are being studied to improve response rates and overcome resistance, which eventually develops in most patients.
why: Dropped 'achieves more complete pathway inhibition and delays resistance' and the melanoma setting, which the quotes do not state; kept the possible synergy and the combination research aimed at overcoming resistance.

evidence.quote: Thus, the synergistic effect of BRAF and MEKis may be observed in RAF-regulated and RAF-dependent variants.

however, resistance eventually develops in most patients after persistent exposure to the drug. Current research focuses on combination strategies with dabrafenib to not only improve response rates but also overcome resistance.

original: In experimental animal models, tumors induced by carcinogens or oncogenic viruses express unique tumor-associated transplantation antigens (TATAs), demonstrating that the immune system can distinguish between normal and transformed cells.
proposed: In experimental animal models, tumors induced by chemical or physical carcinogens usually express unique tumor-specific transplantation antigens that can lead to immune destruction of a transplanted cancer by the host.
why: Narrowed to carcinogen-induced tumors; dropped oncogenic viruses and the 'immune system can distinguish' conclusion. Quote 0 says such antigens are usually unique per tumor; quote 1 shows tumor-specific immunity.

evidence.quote: Tumor-specific transplantation antigens are antigens that can lead to complete immunological destruction of a transplanted cancer by the syngeneic host. When such antigens are expressed on cancers induced by chemical or physical carcinogens, then they are usually unique, i.e., antigenically different for each independently induced tumor.
The therapeutic effect of TSTA was immunologically specific: Animals cured of local MCA-F recurrences promptly died from primary challenge with the non-cross-reacting sarcoma MCA-D.

original: In human cancer patients, the presence of antibodies to tumor-associated antigens (TAAs) and specific effector cells in peripheral circulation has been extensively documented.
proposed: Circulating antibody to a prostate antigen has been reported in patients with prostate cancer.
why: Quote gives one instance (prostate antigen, prostate cancer); dropped general TAAs, effector cells and 'extensively documented'.

evidence.quote: Circulating antibody to prostate antigen in patients with prostate cancer.

original: The loss of MHC Class I expression is particularly significant as it occurs in numerous cancer types and directly prevents recognition by cytotoxic T lymphocytes.
proposed: Loss of MHC class I antigen presentation is a common mechanism of cancer immune escape.
why: Quote 0 calls MHC class I deficiency a common immune escape mechanism; dropped 'numerous cancer types', 'particularly significant' and direct prevention of CTL recognition, which no quote states.

evidence.quote: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I antigen presentation deficiency is a common cancer immune escape mechanism, but the mechanistic implications and potential strategies to address this challenge remain poorly understood.

original: Programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) represents a distinct immune checkpoint with different temporal and spatial functions compared to CTLA-4.
proposed: PD-1 and CTLA-4 are distinct checkpoint receptors: targeting PD-1/PD-L1 can relieve exhaustion of CD8+ T cells, whereas targeting CTLA-4 can renew their priming.
why: Quote distinguishes the two by the T-cell step each targets; temporal and spatial functions are not stated, so replaced with what the quote says.

evidence.quote: Programmed death-1 receptor (PD-1)-ligand (PD-L1) and CTL-associated antigen 4 (CTLA-4) are checkpoint receptors that can be targeted for relieving exhaustion of CD8 + T cells and renewing their priming, respectively, and thereby eliminating antigen-expressing cancer cells.

original: The development and clinical implementation of immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting CTLA-4 and PD-1/PD-L1 pathways have demonstrated that releasing immune system brakes can induce durable, potentially curative responses in patients with advanced cancers that were previously considered terminal.
proposed: Inhibitors of the immune checkpoint proteins CTLA-4, PD-1 and PD-L1 can induce durable remissions in a subset of patients with metastatic disease, including cure in a subset of patients.
why: Quote 1 gives durable remissions in a subset with metastatic disease; quote 0 adds cure in a subset. Dropped 'advanced cancers previously considered terminal' and 'potentially curative' as general claim.

evidence.quote: Immune checkpoint therapy (ICT) has dramatically altered clinical outcomes for cancer patients and conferred durable clinical benefits, including cure in a subset of patients.

Inhibitors of the immune checkpoint proteins cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen (CTLA)-4, programmed death (PD)-1, and PD ligand 1 (PD-L1) can induce durable remissions in a subset of patients with metastatic disease.

original: The success of prophylactic vaccines against HPV and HBV in dramatically reducing the incidence of cervical cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma, respectively, proves that cancer prevention through immunization is achievable and underscores the critical role of the immune system in cancer control.
proposed: After the introduction of HPV vaccination, a substantial reduction in cervical cancer was observed in young women in England, and in Sweden vaccination was associated with a substantially reduced risk of invasive cervical cancer.
why: Quotes cover HPV vaccination and cervical cancer in England and Sweden only; dropped HBV, hepatocellular carcinoma and 'proves'.

evidence.quote: INTERPRETATION: We observed a substantial reduction in cervical cancer and incidence of CIN3 in young women after the introduction of the HPV immunisation programme in England, especially in individuals who were offered the vaccine at age 12-13 years.
CONCLUSIONS: Among Swedish girls and women 10 to 30 years old, quadrivalent HPV vaccination was associated with a substantially reduced risk of invasive cervical cancer at the population level.

module: 26.1 Principles of Gene Therapy for Cancer
original: In the response to DNA damage, p53 activates genes involved in cell-cycle arrest, DNA repair, and induction of apoptosis.

original: AAV-2 is the predominant serotype used in gene therapy approaches.

why: Quote calls AAV2 commonly used and wild-type, in retinal gene therapies; 'predominant' overall is not stated.

evidence.quote: R100 demonstrated superior retinal cell transduction in vitro and in vivo compared to AAV2, a commonly used wild-type AAV serotype in retinal gene therapies.

module: 26.3 Viral Vectors: Mechanisms of Action and Safety
original: Retroviruses are single-stranded RNA viruses that consist of the 5′ and 3′ long-terminal repeats (LTRs) and the gag, pol, and env structural genes.
proposed: Retroviruses have a gag-pol (and env) genome structure.
why: Quote states the shared gag-pol (and env) genome structure; single-stranded RNA and the 5' and 3' LTRs are not stated and were dropped.

evidence.quote: due to their similarity and identical gag-pol (and env) genome structure, it is accepted that they evolve from Ty3/Gypsy LTR retroelements

original: A common theme emerging from studying the interaction of viruses with cells is the presence of viral proteins whose function is to overcome host-cell antiviral defenses.
proposed: Studies of virus-cell interaction have identified viral proteins whose function is to overcome host antiviral defenses, for example adenovirus E4orf4, which inhibits the host DNA damage response, and HSV-1 ICP47, which inhibits TAP to limit CD8+ T-cell recognition.
why: Quotes give two examples (adenovirus E4orf4, HSV-1 ICP47); the claim of a general theme across viruses is replaced by these examples.

evidence.quote: E4orf4 participates in the inhibition of the host DNA damage response, promoting the ability of Ad to counteract this antiviral defense mechanism.
Herpes simplex virus-1 (HSV-1) evades CD8(+) T-cells by producing ICP47, which limits immune recognition of infected cells by inhibiting the transporter associated with antigen processing (TAP).

original: Another technique to achieve tumor-specific cytotoxicity with replication-competent viruses is to place expression of viral essential genes under the transcriptional control of tumor-specific promoter/enhancer sequences.
proposed: One approach with replication-competent viruses is to place expression of the viral E1 gene under a tumor-specific promoter, as in the telomerase-specific replication-competent adenovirus (TRAD), which exhibits efficient antitumor effects.
why: Quote describes TRAD with a tumor-specific promoter-driven E1 cassette and antitumor effects; generalization to 'viral essential genes' and 'enhancer' is dropped.

evidence.quote: the telomerase-specific replication-competent adenovirus (TRAD), which carries the tumor-specific promoter-driven E1 gene expression cassette, exhibits efficient antitumor effects.

G207 is an oncolytic herpes simplex virus (HSV) with deletions at both gamma134.5 loci and a LacZ gene insertion inactivating the HSV ribonucleotide reductase gene.

why: Quotes show the AFP promoter driving retained E1 genes / E1A in vectors for liver cancer cells; 'enhancer' and 'upstream' placement are not stated.

evidence.quote: E1B 55kDa-deleted recombinant adenovirus (YKL-1001), which retained other E1 genes driven by the AFP promoter.
contains only the minimal viral elements required in cis for replication and packaging and the E1 viral genes with E1A under the control of the human alpha-fetoprotein promoter.

Phase I Study to Evaluate Treatment of CRISPR-Cas9 Mediated PD-1 and TCR Gene-knocked Out Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T Cells in Patients With Mesothelin Positive Multiple Solid Tumors.

evidence.quote: Among the CRISPR-Cas technologies that can currently make targeted DNA changes in mammalian cells, prime editors offer an unusual combination of versatility, specificity and precision.

original: Voretigene neparvovec-rzyl was granted approval in December 2017 for treatment of patients with progressive vision loss due to confirmed biallelic mutation in the RPE65 gene.

why: Quotes call efflux transporter overexpression a major / main mechanism among many, not the single predominant or distinct one.

Among the main mechanisms of this multidrug resistance is the overexpression of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters that mediate drug efflux, and, specifically, ABCB1, ABCG2 and ABCC1 are known to cause cancer chemoresistance.

original: Abraxane is a 130-nm, albumin-based nanoparticle formulation of paclitaxel that is clinically used for the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.
proposed: Abraxane is an albumin-bound nanoparticle formulation of paclitaxel with a mean particle size of approximately 130 nanometers.
why: Quote supports the formulation and size; clinical use for metastatic breast cancer is not stated and was dropped.

original: Abraxane was approved by the FDA in 2005 for breast cancer, 2010 for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and 2013 for pancreatic cancer.
proposed: Abraxane was originally approved on 7 January 2005.

evidence.quote: ORIG 1 AP 20050107

proposed: Adsorptive-Mediated Transcytosis (AMT): Transcytosis is triggered by electrostatic interaction between cationic molecules and anionic microdomains on the membrane of brain capillary endothelial cells.

evidence.quote: Many brain drug delivery strategies have focused on adsorptive-mediated transcytosis (AMT), which is triggered by electrostatic interaction between cationic molecules and anionic microdomains on the cytoplasm membrane of the brain capillary endothelial cells.

original: Albumin-bound (nab)-paclitaxel NPs (Abraxane®) were approved in 2012 by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for cancer treatment.
proposed: Albumin-bound (nab)-paclitaxel (Abraxane) was first approved in 2005, with supplemental approvals recorded in 2011 and 2012.
why: Records show original approval 2005-01-07 and supplements approved in Dec 2011 and Oct and Dec 2012; indication and agency are not stated.

evidence.quote: ORIG 1 AP 20050107

original: As drug carriers, polymersomes modify the distribution of drugs in body, prevent drug degradation and inactivation, extend the action time of drugs, and reduce side effects.

why: Quote lists stability, synthesis, circulation time and targeting; protection from degradation, extended action time and reduced side effects are not stated.

why: Carbon-based nanoparticles shown by two examples: gene delivery to melanoma cells and in vivo antitumor efficacy; 'effective in melanoma cells' in general is not stated.

evidence.quote: Additionally, the pH-sensitive material (ppCDs@TMZ) was prepared by coating PAE-PEG (pp) onto CDs@TMZ and achieving remarkable antitumor efficacy in vivo without significant toxicity on normal tissues.
The studies show that the as-designed GEMNS-PEI construct is successfully used to transfect the melanoma cells with pDNA

evidence.quote: Ovarian cancer: After failure of platinum-based chemotherapy ( 1.1 ) • AIDS-related Kaposi’s Sarcoma: After failure of prior systemic chemotherapy or intolerance to such therapy ( 1.2 ) • Multiple Myeloma: In combination with bortezomib in patients who have not previously received bortezomib and have received at least one prior therapy ( 1.3 )

original: In melanoma models, phosphatidylethanolamine liposomal cisplatin was proven to have higher cytotoxicity than classic liposomes or free cisplatin, maintaining high intratumoral drug concentration for 72 hours and efficiently delivering 3.6-times more drug compared to the free drug.
proposed: PE liposomes were reported to have higher cytotoxicity than classic liposomes or free cisplatin; with intratumoral administration in vivo, the cisplatin concentration in tumor tissue stayed high for 72 hours, and PE liposomes delivered approximately 3.6 times more cisplatin into the tumor than the free drug.
why: Both quotes support the comparisons; melanoma models are not named and 'proven' is softened to 'reported'.

evidence.quote: PE liposomes had higher cytotoxicity than classic liposomes or free cisplatin.

With in vivo intratumoral administration, the cisplatin concentration in the tumor tissue was maintained at a high level for 72 h after application of the PE liposomes. The PE liposomes delivered cisplatin into the tumor approximately 3.6 times more efficiently than the free drug.

original: In the context of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the surrounding brain parenchyma consists of a dense matrix which gives rise to elevated interstitial pressure, further limiting nanoparticle penetration.
proposed: In glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), high interstitial pressure and a dense extracellular matrix hinder drug penetration, and the aberrant extracellular matrix appears to drive interstitial fluid pressure-related drug efflux, contributing to insufficient penetration of nano-sized therapeutics.
why: Quotes tie dense ECM and high interstitial pressure to poor penetration in GBM; 'surrounding brain parenchyma' is not stated.

evidence.quote: which includes high interstitial pressure, abnormal vasculature, and dense extracellular matrix that together hinder drug penetration and distribution.

The pathological and physiological barriers of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) lead to insufficient extravasation and penetration of nano-sized therapeutics. As the main driver of interstitial fluid pressure-related drug efflux, the aberrant extracellular matrix (ECM) appears to be a valuable target that plays a crucial role in forming pathological barriers of GBM.

original: Lipid Bilayer Composition : The liposome lipid bilayer exists in a "liquid ordered" phase composed of high-Tm (53 °C) phosphatidylcholine and cholesterol, providing enhanced stability and controlled drug release.
proposed: In one liposome design, the lipid bilayer is in a "liquid ordered" phase composed of high-Tm (53 °C) phosphatidylcholine and cholesterol.
why: Quote describes this bilayer as one feature of a design; enhanced stability and controlled drug release are not stated and were dropped.

evidence.quote: (iii) having the liposome lipid bilayer in a "liquid ordered" phase composed of the high-T(m) (53 °C) phosphatidylcholine, and cholesterol.

original: SPARC-Mediated Release : In the tumoral interstitium, SPARC (secreted protein, acidic and rich in cysteine) is selectively secreted by the tumors and binds to albumin-bound paclitaxel with the resultant release of paclitaxel in the vicinity of tumor cells.
proposed: Albumin binding to secreted protein acidic and rich in cysteine (SPARC) has been proposed as a contributing factor to the tumor accumulation of nab-paclitaxel, although supporting data remain largely correlative.
why: Quotes describe an albumin-SPARC interaction, called possible and correlative; selective tumor secretion and drug release near tumor cells are not stated.

evidence.quote: Another possible contributing factor to the tumor accumulation of nab-paclitaxel is the binding of albumin to secreted protein acidic and rich in cysteine (SPARC), although the data supporting this relationship between SPARC and nab-paclitaxel remain largely correlative at this point.
Nano albumin bound (Nab)-paclitaxel is an innovative molecule depleting tumor stroma, through interaction between albumin and secreted protein acidic and rich in cysteine.

original: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) constitutes a microvascular network responsible for excluding most drugs from the brain, representing one of the most formidable challenges in nanomedicine.
proposed: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) complicates pharmacotherapy for CNS disorders, as most chemical drugs and biopharmaceuticals are impeded from entering the brain.
why: Quote supports the impeded drug entry; the microvascular description and 'one of the most formidable challenges in nanomedicine' are not stated.

evidence.quote: However, the presence of BBB complicates the pharmacotherapy for CNS disorders as the most chemical drugs and biopharmaceuticals have been impeded to enter the brain.

original: The protein corona spontaneously develops and evolves on the surface of nanoscale materials when they are exposed to biological environments, altering their physiochemical properties and affecting their subsequent interactions with biosystems.
